Im Zweiten Weltkrieg wurde das Gebäude stark beschädigt, aber in den 1950er Jahren wurde es wieder aufgebaut. 2019 wurde der Bahnhof renoviert. Heute wird er jeden Tag von etwa 20.000 Menschen benutzt." When was the station rebuilt?
questions.explanation: "in den 1950er Jahren wurde es wieder aufgebaut": it was rebuilt in the 1950s. 1872 is when it was opened, during the war it was damaged, and in 2019 it was renovated.

questions.stem: A headline says: "Rathaus nach Brand geschlossen". What does it mean?
choices: The town hall has been closed after a fire.
The town hall closed the fire.
The town hall will be closed after a fire.
A fire closed the town hall's door.
questions.explanation: Headlines leave out the auxiliary verb, so the participle stands alone: "Rathaus nach Brand geschlossen" = "Das Rathaus ist nach dem Brand geschlossen worden." Nothing points to the future, and the town hall isn't the one doing the closing.

questions.stem: Complete: "Das Formular muss bis Freitag ___."
questions.explanation: After a modal verb, the passive infinitive goes to the end: participle + werden, "unterschrieben werden". "worden" belongs to the Perfekt passive only, "wird" can't follow a modal, and "unterschreiben werden" uses the infinitive instead of the participle.

questions.stem: A sign means "Bikes may not be parked here". Complete: "Fahrräder ___ hier nicht abgestellt werden."
questions.explanation: A ban is nicht dürfen, and the modal agrees with the plural subject "Fahrräder": "dürfen". "darf" is singular. "müssen nicht" would mean bikes don't have to be parked here, and "dürften" is Konjunktiv II.

questions.stem: What does "Der Antrag muss nicht persönlich abgegeben werden." mean?
choices: The application must not be handed in in person.
The application must be handed in in person.
The application doesn't have to be handed in in person.
The application can't be handed in.
questions.explanation: nicht müssen means "not have to": you may hand it in in person, but you don't need to. English "must not" (a ban) is nicht dürfen in German: "darf nicht persönlich abgegeben werden".

questions.stem: Complete: "Im Brief steht, dass die Gebühr bis Ende Mai ___."
questions.explanation: In a subordinate clause the conjugated modal goes to the very end, after the passive infinitive: participle + werden + modal, "bezahlt werden muss". "muss bezahlt werden" is main-clause order.

questions.stem: Complete: "Wegen des Unfalls ___ die Straße gestern gesperrt werden."
questions.explanation: For the past, use the Präteritum of the modal: "musste … gesperrt werden" (had to be closed). "muss" is present, and neither "hat" nor "wurde" can be followed by "gesperrt werden".

questions.stem: On a form you read: "Der Ausweis ist auf Verlangen vorzulegen." What does it mean?
choices: You must show your ID on request.
You can show your ID if you want to.
Your ID will be sent to you on request.
questions.explanation: sein + zu + infinitive in rules and official texts means "must be done": "ist vorzulegen" = "muss vorgelegt werden". With separable verbs, zu goes between the prefix and the verb: vor-zu-legen.

questions.stem: Which sentence means the same as "Das Problem ist leicht zu lösen."?
choices: Das Problem muss leicht gelöst werden.
Das Problem kann leicht gelöst werden.
Das Problem ist leicht gelöst worden.
questions.explanation: With words like leicht, schwer or kaum, sein + zu means "can be done": the problem can easily be solved. It says nothing about the past, so "wurde gelöst" and "ist gelöst worden" are wrong, and "muss leicht gelöst werden" makes no sense.

questions.stem: What does "Die Wohnung ist für uns nicht bezahlbar." mean?
choices: We haven't paid for the flat yet.
We don't have to pay for the flat.
The flat is free for us.
questions.explanation: -bar means "can be …-ed": bezahlbar = kann bezahlt werden, affordable. "nicht bezahlbar" means it can't be paid for by us: we can't afford it.

questions.stem: Read: "Stadtbibliothek – Hinweise: Bücher können bis zu vier Wochen ausgeliehen werden. Die Ausleihe kann zweimal online verlängert werden. Für verspätete Rückgaben muss eine Gebühr von 50 Cent pro Tag bezahlt werden. Im Lesesaal darf nicht gegessen werden; Getränke in Flaschen sind erlaubt. Taschen und Jacken müssen im Erdgeschoss gelassen werden." Which of these is allowed in the reading room?
questions.explanation: "Getränke in Flaschen sind erlaubt": drinks in bottles are allowed. Eating is not (darf nicht gegessen werden), and bags and jackets must be left on the ground floor (müssen im Erdgeschoss gelassen werden).

questions.stem: Read the library notice again: "Bücher können bis zu vier Wochen ausgeliehen werden. Die Ausleihe kann zweimal online verlängert werden. Für verspätete Rückgaben muss eine Gebühr von 50 Cent pro Tag bezahlt werden." You return a book three days late. What happens?
choices: Nothing, because you can extend online.
You can't borrow books any more.
questions.explanation: A fee of 50 cents per day must be paid (muss bezahlt werden): three days × 50 cents = 1.50 euros. Extending online (verlängern) only helps before the book is late, and the notice says nothing about a ban.

questions.stem: Which word fits? "Wer falsch parkt, muss ein ___ bezahlen."
questions.explanation: das Bußgeld is a fine for a minor offence such as parking in the wrong place. das Gesetz is a law, die Genehmigung a permit (and feminine, so "eine"), and der Nachweis is proof.

questions.stem: Which sign means "Keep off the grass"?
choices: Der Rasen muss nicht betreten werden.
Der Rasen darf nicht betreten werden.
questions.explanation: A ban is nicht dürfen: "darf nicht betreten werden" (may not be walked on). "muss nicht" only says it isn't necessary, "kann betreten werden" allows it, and "wird nicht betreten" just describes what happens.

questions.stem: Complete: "Freust du dich auf die Ferien?" – "Ja, ich freue mich sehr ___."
questions.explanation: sich freuen auf (to look forward to) keeps its preposition, and for a thing (die Ferien) you replace "auf + noun" with the da-compound "darauf". "auf sie" is for people, "darüber" belongs to sich freuen über (pleased about), and "worauf" is a question word.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ hast du Angst?" – "Vor Gewittern."
questions.explanation: Angst haben vor: to ask about a thing (thunderstorms), use wo + vor = "Wovor". "Vor wem" asks about a person, "Davor" is not a question word, and "Wofür" has the wrong preposition.

questions.stem: Complete: "Wartest du auf deinen Bruder?" – "Ja, ich warte ___."
questions.explanation: For a person, don't use a da-compound: use the preposition + pronoun. warten auf takes the accusative, so "auf ihn". "darauf" would refer to a thing, and "auf ihm" is dative.

questions.stem: Complete: "Es kommt ___ an, ob das Wetter gut ist."
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is "es kommt darauf an" (it depends). The da-compound points ahead to the ob-clause. "davon" goes with "es hängt davon ab, ob …", which means the same but uses a different verb.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ich bin ___, dass Handys in der Schule verboten werden."
questions.explanation: To say you are in favour of something expressed by a whole clause, German puts the da-compound before it: "Ich bin dafür, dass …". "für" alone can't introduce a dass-clause, and "darüber" and "dazu" don't go with sein in this meaning.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ich halte das ___ eine gute Idee."
questions.explanation: "halten für" + accusative means "to consider, think something is": "Ich halte das für eine gute Idee." English "regard as" tempts learners to use "als", but halten always takes für in this meaning.

questions.stem: Your friend says: "Ich finde, man sollte soziale Medien für Kinder ganz verbieten." Which reply partly agrees?
choices: Da hast du zwar recht, aber ein Verbot hilft meiner Meinung nach wenig.
questions.explanation: "Da hast du zwar recht, aber …" accepts part of the point and then adds a different view. "Genau, das sehe ich genauso" agrees completely, "Da muss ich dir widersprechen" disagrees, and "Das ist mir egal" shows no opinion.

questions.stem: Complete: "Da muss ich ___ widersprechen."
questions.explanation: widersprechen takes the dative, like zustimmen: "Ich widerspreche dir. Ich stimme dir zu." "dich" is accusative, the case English speakers expect after "contradict you".

questions.stem: Read: "Ich lese Nachrichten fast nur noch in den sozialen Medien. Das ist praktisch, aber ich sehe dort oft Falschmeldungen. Letzte Woche wurde ein Beitrag über einen angeblichen Stromausfall tausendmal geteilt. Ich habe die Quelle überprüft: Es war eine Lüge. Seitdem lese ich jeden Morgen wieder eine Zeitung online." What has the writer done since last week?
choices: Read an online newspaper every morning
Shared the post about the power cut
questions.explanation: "Seitdem lese ich jeden Morgen wieder eine Zeitung online": since then the writer has been reading an online newspaper every morning again. The text doesn't say they stopped using social media, and they checked the post rather than sharing it.

questions.stem: In the same post, what does "ein Beitrag über einen angeblichen Stromausfall" tell you about the power cut?
choices: It was only claimed; it may not be true.
It was reported by a newspaper.
questions.explanation: angeblich means "supposedly, allegedly": somebody claimed there was a power cut, but it isn't confirmed. In fact the writer then found out it was a lie (eine Lüge).

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Meiner Meinung nach soziale Medien sind gefährlich.
Meiner Meinung nach, ich finde soziale Medien gefährlich.
Nach meiner Meinung soziale Medien gefährlich sind.
Meiner Meinung nach sind soziale Medien gefährlich.
questions.explanation: "Meiner Meinung nach" fills position 1, so the verb comes straight after it: "Meiner Meinung nach sind …". It isn't followed by a comma and a new main clause, and it doesn't send the verb to the end.

questions.stem: Complete: "Das ist etwas, ___ ich mich sehr freue."
questions.explanation: After etwas, the relative pronoun is was, but when the verb needs a preposition (sich freuen über), was becomes a wo-compound: "worüber". Plain "was" leaves out the preposition, "darüber" can't start a relative clause, and "über den" is a masculine relative pronoun, which doesn't refer back to etwas.

questions.stem: Complete: "Der Bundestag wird alle vier Jahre ___."
questions.explanation: Present passive: wird + participle, "wird gewählt" (is elected). "wählen" is the infinitive, which would make it future active, and "gewählt worden" needs ist. You abstimmen over a question, but you wählen a parliament.

questions.stem: Complete: "Im Parlament wird morgen über das neue Gesetz ___."
questions.explanation: To vote on a question or a law is "abstimmen über": "Es wird über das Gesetz abgestimmt." wählen is for people and parties. "zugestimmt worden" is the Perfekt and doesn't fit with "morgen".

questions.stem: Complete: "Heute Abend gehe ich auf eine ___ bei meiner Freundin. Es gibt Musik und Pizza."
questions.explanation: A party with music and food is "die Party" (or die Feier). "die Partei" is only a political party, a common mix-up for English speakers.

questions.stem: What does "nach der Einführung des Gesetzes" mean?
choices: after the introduction to the law (a text)
questions.explanation: This is nominal style: the noun Einführung stands for the verb einführen, and the genitive "des Gesetzes" is its object. Turned back into a clause: "nachdem das Gesetz eingeführt worden war" – after the law was introduced.

questions.stem: Which sentence means the same as "Die Regierung plant die Erhöhung der Steuern."?
choices: Die Regierung hat die Steuern schon erhöht.
Die Regierung plant, die Steuern zu erhöhen.
Die Regierung wird von den Steuern erhöht.
questions.explanation: die Erhöhung der Steuern = die Steuern erhöhen: the government is planning to raise taxes. It hasn't done it yet (plant), and the taxes are the object, not the subject.

questions.stem: Complete: "Die Politikerin, ___ viele junge Leute vertrauen, ist erst 30 Jahre alt."
questions.explanation: vertrauen takes the dative (jemandem vertrauen), and Politikerin is feminine singular, so the relative pronoun is "der". "die" is nominative or accusative, and "denen" is dative plural.

questions.stem: Complete: "Das Grundgesetz schützt die Rechte ___ Bürger."
questions.explanation: "die Bürger" (plural) in the genitive is "der Bürger": the rights of the citizens. "des" is masculine or neuter singular, which would need "des Bürgers".

questions.stem: Read: "In der Schweiz wählen die Bürgerinnen und Bürger nicht nur Parteien. Mehrmals im Jahr wird auch direkt über wichtige Fragen abgestimmt, zum Beispiel über neue Gesetze oder Steuern. So eine Abstimmung heißt Volksabstimmung. Viele Schweizer finden dieses System sehr demokratisch. Kritiker sagen aber, dass manche Themen für eine Abstimmung zu kompliziert sind." What is a Volksabstimmung?
choices: An election in which people choose a party
A demonstration in front of parliament
A vote in which citizens decide a question directly
questions.explanation: The text says people vote directly on important questions (direkt über wichtige Fragen abgestimmt), and this is called a Volksabstimmung. Choosing parties is a Wahl.

questions.stem: In the same text about Switzerland, what do the critics say?
choices: There are too few votes each year.
Some topics are too complicated for a vote.
Only parties should decide about taxes.
questions.explanation: "Kritiker sagen aber, dass manche Themen für eine Abstimmung zu kompliziert sind": some topics are too complicated to be decided by a vote. It is the supporters who call the system very democratic.

questions.stem: Read: "Ich heiße Tarek, bin 24 und studiere Informatik. Seit zwei Jahren engagiere ich mich in einem Sprachcafé. Dort treffen sich jeden Donnerstag Menschen, die Deutsch lernen, mit Menschen, die Deutsch als Muttersprache sprechen. Für die Integration ist das sehr wichtig. Ich mache das ehrenamtlich, aber ich habe viele neue Freunde gefunden." Which statement is true?
choices: Tarek isn't paid for his work in the language café.
Tarek works as a German teacher.
questions.explanation: ehrenamtlich means voluntary and unpaid. Tarek studies computer science, the café meets on Thursdays, and he has been involved for two years (seit zwei Jahren).

questions.stem: According to the lesson, who elects the Federal Chancellor (Bundeskanzler) in Germany?
choices: The governments of the federal states
questions.explanation: The people elect the Bundestag; after a coalition has been formed, the members of the Bundestag (die Abgeordneten) elect the Chancellor. The Federal President is the head of state and appoints the ministers.

questions.stem: What does "Nach der Wahl des neuen Bürgermeisters gab es ein Fest." mean?
choices: After the new mayor chose a party, there was a celebration.
Before the new mayor was elected, there was a party.
The new mayor voted after the party.
After the new mayor had been elected, there was a party.
questions.explanation: "die Wahl des neuen Bürgermeisters" is nominal style for "der neue Bürgermeister wurde gewählt": the mayor is the one being elected, not the one choosing. "nach" means after, not before.

questions.stem: Complete: "Wenn ich mehr Zeit ___, würde ich öfter kochen."
questions.explanation: An unreal condition needs the Konjunktiv II in the wenn clause too. For haben the form is "hätte". "habe" is the indicative (a real condition), "hatte" is the simple past, and "würde haben" is avoided with haben.

questions.stem: What is the Konjunktiv II of "kommen" for "er"?
questions.explanation: Strong verbs form the Konjunktiv II from the simple past stem (kam) plus an umlaut and -e: käme. "kam" is just the simple past, "kommte" doesn't exist, and after würde the verb must be an infinitive (würde kommen).

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Wenn ich reich wäre, würde ich ein Haus kaufen.
Wenn ich reich wäre, ich würde ein Haus kaufen.
Wenn ich wäre reich, würde ich ein Haus kaufen.
Wenn ich reich bin, würde ich ein Haus kaufen.
questions.explanation: The wenn clause has the verb at the end (reich wäre) and counts as position 1, so the main clause starts with its verb: würde ich. Putting "ich" first copies English word order, and "wenn ich reich bin" is the indicative, which doesn't match an imagined result.

questions.stem: Which sentence means the same as "Wenn ich ein Auto hätte, würde ich dich abholen."?
choices: Ich hatte ein Auto, deshalb habe ich dich abgeholt.
Hätte ich ein Auto, würde ich dich abholen.
Wenn ich ein Auto habe, hole ich dich ab.
Ich hätte ein Auto, aber ich würde dich abholen.
questions.explanation: An unreal condition can drop wenn if the verb moves to the front: "Hätte ich ein Auto, …". The other sentences describe real past events, a real possibility (indicative) or something else entirely.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ich ___ dir gern helfen, aber ich habe heute keine Zeit."
questions.explanation: The speaker is imagining something that won't happen, so the modal goes into the Konjunktiv II: könnte (with umlaut). "konnte" without the umlaut is the simple past, "kann" states a fact, and modals don't use würde.

questions.stem: Which version sounds most natural in everyday German?
choices: Wenn ich nach Japan fliegen würde, …
Wenn ich nach Japan geflogen würde, …
questions.explanation: For most verbs, spoken German uses würde + infinitive. "flöge" is correct but sounds old-fashioned or literary. "flog" is the simple past, and würde can't be combined with a participle.

questions.stem: Read: "Tom arbeitet in einer Bank in Frankfurt. Er verdient gut, aber er hat kaum Freizeit. Wenn er könnte, würde er nach Portugal auswandern und dort ein kleines Café eröffnen. Leider spricht er kein Portugiesisch, und seine Freundin möchte in Deutschland bleiben. Vielleicht macht er erst einmal einen Sprachkurs." Which statement is true?
choices: Tom would like to emigrate, but there are obstacles.
Tom's girlfriend wants to move to Portugal.
questions.explanation: "Wenn er könnte, würde er … auswandern" is an unreal condition: it's his dream, not reality. The language and his girlfriend, who wants to stay in Germany, are the obstacles. He hasn't moved or opened a café.

questions.stem: What does "ausgerechnet" mean in "Ausgerechnet heute ist mein Fahrrad kaputt!"?
questions.explanation: "ausgerechnet" expresses annoyance or surprise that something happens at the worst possible time or to the most unlikely person: today of all days. It has nothing to do with counting (rechnen) in this use.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ich stelle ___ das Leben auf dem Land sehr ruhig vor."
questions.explanation: "sich vorstellen" in the sense of "to imagine" takes a dative reflexive pronoun because there is already an accusative object (das Leben): ich stelle mir etwas vor. "Ich stelle mich vor" means "I introduce myself".

questions.stem: Which is the Konjunktiv II of "wissen" for "ich"?
questions.explanation: "wissen" is a mixed verb: simple past wusste, plus umlaut gives wüsste ("Wenn ich das wüsste!"). "wusste" is the simple past, "weiß" the present, and "wisste" doesn't exist.

questions.stem: A: "Was würdest du machen, wenn du ein Jahr frei hättest?" B: "___"
choices: Ich bin um die Welt gereist.
Ich reise um die Welt, wenn ich Zeit gehabt habe.
Ich hätte um die Welt reisen.
Ich würde um die Welt reisen.
questions.explanation: The question is about an imagined situation, so the answer uses the Konjunktiv II: würde + infinitive. The perfect describes something that really happened, and "hätte" needs a participle, not an infinitive.

questions.stem: Which sentence contains a mistake?
choices: Wäre das Wetter schön, könnten wir grillen.
Wenn du mehr schlafen würdest, wärst du nicht so müde.
Wenn ich konnte, würde ich dir helfen.
Es gäbe weniger Stau, wenn mehr Leute Rad fahren würden.
questions.explanation: Without the umlaut, "konnte" is the simple past ("I was able to"). An unreal condition needs "könnte": Wenn ich könnte, würde ich dir helfen. The other three sentences are correct unreal conditions.

questions.stem: Which word fits? "Meine Arbeit ist sehr ___: Jeder Tag ist anders."
questions.explanation: "abwechslungsreich" means varied, full of variety, which matches "every day is different". "langweilig" (boring) is the opposite; "unabhängig" (independent) and "ehrgeizig" (ambitious) describe people, not a job's variety.

questions.stem: Complete: "Wenn ich das gewusst hätte, ___ ich zu Hause geblieben."
questions.explanation: "bleiben" forms the perfect with sein (ist geblieben), so the past subjunctive uses wäre: wäre geblieben. "hätte geblieben" is the classic auxiliary mistake, and "würde geblieben" is not a German form.

questions.stem: Complete: "Wenn du mich gefragt ___, hätte ich dir geholfen."
questions.explanation: The wenn clause also needs the past subjunctive, and fragen takes haben: du hättest gefragt. "hast" would be the indicative perfect, "würdest" can't go with a participle, and fragen doesn't take sein.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: With a modal and another verb, the past subjunctive uses hätte + two infinitives (the double infinitive): hätte … losfahren sollen. The modal stays in the infinitive, and it always takes hätte, even though losfahren itself takes sein.

questions.stem: What does "Du hättest mich anrufen können!" express?
choices: a request: could you call me?
a fact: you were able to call me
a reproach: you could have called me (but didn't)
a plan: you will call me later
questions.explanation: "hätte … können" refers to a possibility in the past that wasn't used. Said with an exclamation mark, it is a reproach. A request for now would be "Könntest du mich anrufen?"

questions.stem: Which sentence describes something that almost happened but didn't?
questions.explanation: beinahe (or fast) + past subjunctive describes a near miss: "Ich wäre beinahe gefallen" means I almost fell, so I didn't. "Ich bin gefallen" says it did happen; the others are present or hypothetical.

questions.stem: Complete the mixed sentence: "Wenn ich gestern nicht so lange gefeiert hätte, ___ ich jetzt nicht so müde."
questions.explanation: The condition is in the past, but the result is about now (jetzt), so the main clause takes the present Konjunktiv II: wäre. "wäre gewesen" would put the tiredness in the past, and "bin" is the indicative.

questions.stem: Read: "Letztes Jahr bekam Sara ein Jobangebot in Zürich. Sie hat es abgelehnt, weil sie ihre Familie nicht verlassen wollte. Ein Jahr später hat die Firma in Zürich zugemacht. Rückblickend ist Sara sehr erleichtert. Wenn sie umgezogen wäre, hätte sie jetzt keine Arbeit." How does Sara feel about her decision today?
choices: She regrets turning the job down.
She is relieved that she turned the job down.
She is angry with her family.
She is looking for a job in Zürich.
questions.explanation: "Rückblickend ist Sara sehr erleichtert": looking back, she is relieved. The past subjunctive "Wenn sie umgezogen wäre, hätte sie jetzt keine Arbeit" explains why: the company closed, so moving would have left her without work.

questions.stem: What does "im Nachhinein" mean?
questions.explanation: "im Nachhinein" (also "rückblickend" or "hinterher") means in hindsight, afterwards. "in advance" is "im Voraus".

questions.stem: Which sentence contains a mistake?
choices: Wenn ich den Bus nicht verpasst hätte, wäre ich pünktlich gewesen.
Hätte ich den Bus nicht verpasst, wäre ich pünktlich gewesen.
Ohne den Stau wäre ich pünktlich gewesen.
Wenn ich den Bus nicht verpasst habe, wäre ich pünktlich gewesen.
questions.explanation: The wenn clause of an unreal past condition also needs the past subjunctive: verpasst hätte, not verpasst habe. The other three are correct: with wenn, without wenn (verb first), and with ohne + noun replacing the condition.

questions.stem: Complete: "Das war nicht deine ___, du konntest nichts dafür."
questions.explanation: "Das ist meine/deine Schuld" means that's my/your fault. "die Ursache" is a cause (of an event, not a person's blame), "die Wirkung" is an effect and "die Reue" is remorse.

questions.stem: Which verb fits? "Mit einem Helm hätte man die Verletzung ___ können."
questions.explanation: "verhindern" means to prevent: with a helmet the injury could have been prevented. "verursachen" (to cause) is the opposite, "bereuen" (to regret) and "versäumen" (to miss) don't fit.

questions.stem: A: "Warum bist du nicht zur Party gekommen?" B: "Ich war krank. ___"
questions.explanation: B imagines a past that didn't happen, so the past subjunctive is needed. "kommen" takes sein in the perfect (ist gekommen), so it's "wäre gekommen". "würde gekommen" doesn't exist.

questions.stem: Complete the wish: "Wenn ich nur mehr Geld ___!"
questions.explanation: An unreal wish uses the Konjunktiv II with nur, doch or bloß, verb at the end: Wenn ich nur mehr Geld hätte! The indicative "habe" would not express a wish, "hatte" (no umlaut) is the simple past, and "hättest" is the du form.

questions.stem: Which sentence is a wish about the past?
choices: Hätte ich das bloß nicht gesagt!
questions.explanation: A wish about the past uses the past subjunctive (hätte/wäre + participle): Hätte ich das bloß nicht gesagt! (If only I hadn't said that!) The other three wish for something different now.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: An deiner Stelle ich würde mit ihm reden.
An deiner Stelle würde ich mit ihm reden.
An deiner Stelle würde ich mit ihm reden würden.
In deiner Stelle würde ich mit ihm reden.
questions.explanation: "an deiner Stelle" fills position 1, so the verb comes next: würde ich. The preposition is an, not in, and würde appears only once, with the infinitive at the end.

questions.stem: Which request is the most polite?
choices: Halten Sie mir die Tür auf!
Können Sie mir die Tür aufhalten?
Wären Sie so nett, mir die Tür aufzuhalten?
Sie halten mir die Tür auf, ja?
questions.explanation: "Wären Sie so nett, … zu …?" uses the Konjunktiv II and is very polite. The imperative is direct, "Können Sie" is polite but less so, and the last version sounds like an order.

questions.stem: Complete: "Würde es Ihnen etwas ausmachen, das Fenster ___?"
questions.explanation: "Würde es Ihnen etwas ausmachen" is followed by a zu-infinitive at the end: das Fenster zu schließen. zu comes directly before the infinitive.

questions.stem: Which sentence gives advice (not a reproach)?
choices: Du hättest mehr Wasser trinken sollen.
Du hast zu wenig Wasser getrunken.
questions.explanation: "Du solltest …" is advice for now or the future. "Du hättest … sollen" refers to the past: it's too late, so it sounds like a reproach. The other two are statements or questions about the past.

questions.stem: Read: "Liebe Frau Lindner, meine beste Freundin ist vor drei Monaten nach Australien gezogen. Seitdem fühle ich mich einsam. Wir schreiben uns zwar oft, aber das ist nicht dasselbe. Ich traue mich nicht, in einen Verein zu gehen, weil ich dort niemanden kenne. Was soll ich tun? Mia" What is Mia's problem?
choices: She wants to move to Australia.
She has had an argument with her best friend.
She has too little time for her hobbies.
She feels lonely and is too shy to meet new people.
questions.explanation: Mia says "fühle ich mich einsam" (I feel lonely) and "Ich traue mich nicht, in einen Verein zu gehen" (I don't dare join a club). Her friend moved away; there was no argument, and Mia doesn't say she wants to move.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Ich wünschte, dass du wärst hier.
questions.explanation: An unreal wish with "Ich wünschte" (the Konjunktiv II of wünschen) is followed by a clause in the Konjunktiv II: du wärst hier. "Ich wünsche" is for good wishes (Ich wünsche dir Glück); a dass clause would need the verb at the end.

questions.stem: What does "Er tut so, als ob er krank wäre." mean?
choices: He is ill, so he stays at home.
He would be ill if he went out.
He asks whether he is ill.
He acts as if he were ill (but he isn't).
questions.explanation: "als ob" + Konjunktiv II is an unreal comparison: it describes how someone seems or behaves, while suggesting it isn't true. "so tun, als ob" means to act as if, to pretend.

questions.stem: Which sentence has the same meaning as "Sie sieht aus, als ob sie nicht geschlafen hätte."?
choices: Sie sieht aus, als hätte sie nicht geschlafen.
Sie sieht aus, als ob hätte sie nicht geschlafen.
Sie sieht aus, als sie nicht geschlafen hätte.
Sie sieht aus, ob sie nicht geschlafen hätte.
questions.explanation: The short form of "als ob" is "als" with the conjugated verb straight after it: als hätte sie nicht geschlafen. With als ob, the verb goes to the end; you can't mix the two orders.

questions.stem: What does "schüchtern" mean?
questions.explanation: "schüchtern" means shy. Brave is "mutig", desperate is "verzweifelt" and lonely is "einsam".

questions.stem: Complete: "Auf meine Kollegen kann ich mich immer ___."
questions.explanation: "sich verlassen auf + accusative" means to rely on. "sich trauen" means to dare, "unterstützen" (to support) takes a direct object without auf, and "trösten" means to comfort.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ob wir grillen, hängt ___ Wetter ab."
questions.explanation: "abhängen von + dative" means to depend on: vom (von dem) Wetter. English "depend on" tempts learners to use auf, but German uses von.

questions.stem: Complete: "Wir sind sehr stolz ___ unsere Tochter."
questions.explanation: "stolz auf + accusative" means proud of. English "proud of" leads many learners to "von", which is wrong here.

questions.stem: Complete: "Bist du mit ___ neuen Job zufrieden?"
questions.explanation: "zufrieden mit" takes the dative, because mit is always dative. "Job" is masculine, so it's "mit deinem neuen Job".

questions.stem: Which is correct?
choices: Sie hat großes Interesse an Kunst.
Sie hat großes Interesse über Kunst.
Sie hat großes Interesse in Kunst.
Sie hat großes Interesse auf Kunst.
questions.explanation: The noun "das Interesse" takes an + dative (Interesse an etwas haben), although the verb is "sich interessieren für"; für only appears with zeigen (Interesse für etwas zeigen). This is one of the nouns whose preposition differs from the verb's.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ich zweifle an ___ Ehrlichkeit."
questions.explanation: "zweifeln an" takes the dative: an seiner Ehrlichkeit (Ehrlichkeit is feminine). an is a two-way preposition, and in this fixed phrase it is dative, unlike "denken an" + accusative.

questions.stem: Ask about the thing in standard German: "Ich habe mich über den Preis gewundert."
choices: Über was hast du dich gewundert?
Über wen hast du dich gewundert?
questions.explanation: For a thing in a prepositional object, standard German uses wo(r)- + preposition: worüber. "Über was" is heard in casual speech but isn't the standard form, "über wen" is for people, and the question can't drop the preposition.

questions.stem: Ask about the person: "Sie sorgt sich um ihren Vater."
questions.explanation: For a person, keep the preposition and add wen (accusative) or wem (dative). um takes the accusative, so it's "Um wen". "Worum" would ask about a thing.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Es hängt ab, ob ich Zeit habe.
Es hängt davon ab, ich Zeit habe.
Es hängt von ab, ob ich Zeit habe.
Es hängt davon ab, ob ich Zeit habe.
questions.explanation: When a prepositional verb is followed by a clause, the da-word points ahead to it: davon ab, ob … The preposition can't stand alone, and the ob clause needs its conjunction.

questions.stem: Read: "Herr Brandt ist 72 und begeistert von Computern. Jeden Dienstag geht er in einen Kurs für Senioren. Er beschäftigt sich vor allem mit Fotos: Er sortiert und bearbeitet alte Familienbilder. Seine Enkel sind stolz auf ihn, aber sie wundern sich manchmal, wie viel Zeit er vor dem Bildschirm verbringt." Which statement is true?
choices: Herr Brandt's grandchildren are worried about his health.
Herr Brandt teaches a computer course.
Herr Brandt spends a lot of time working on family photos.
Herr Brandt isn't interested in computers.
questions.explanation: "Er beschäftigt sich vor allem mit Fotos … bearbeitet alte Familienbilder" and the grandchildren are surprised how much time he spends at the screen. He attends the course (he doesn't teach it), and "begeistert von" means he's enthusiastic, not uninterested.

questions.stem: What does "Ich bin gespannt auf den neuen Film." mean?
choices: I'm disappointed by the new film.
I can't wait to see the new film.
I'm tired of the new film.
I'm afraid of the new film.
questions.explanation: "gespannt auf" describes eager, curious anticipation: I'm excited to see it. Disappointed is "enttäuscht von", afraid is "Angst haben vor".

questions.stem: Complete: "I'm Urlaub verzichte ich ___ mein Handy."
questions.explanation: "verzichten auf + accusative" means to do without, give up. "ohne" means without, but it isn't used with verzichten.

questions.stem: Complete: "Die Prüfung besteht ___ drei Teilen."
questions.explanation: "bestehen aus + dative" means to consist of: aus drei Teilen (dative plural with -n). English "consist of" may suggest von, but German uses aus.

questions.stem: Complete: "Die neue Kollegin scheint sehr nett ___."
questions.explanation: "scheinen" (to seem) is used with zu + infinitive at the end: Sie scheint nett zu sein. Without zu, the sentence is wrong.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "You don't have to bring anything."?
questions.explanation: "brauchen nicht/nichts/kein … zu" is the negative of müssen: no need to. "Du darfst nichts mitbringen" means you're not allowed to bring anything. With a separable verb, zu goes between the prefix and the verb: mitzubringen.

questions.stem: What is the gender of "Beförderung"?
questions.explanation: Nouns ending in -ung are always feminine: die Beförderung, die Leitung, die Bewerbung.

questions.stem: Which noun is NOT feminine?
questions.explanation: Nouns ending in -um are neuter: das Zentrum. -keit (die Arbeitslosigkeit) and -schaft (die Gewerkschaft) are always feminine, and -ion nouns like die Qualifikation practically always are.

questions.stem: Who is "der Arbeitgeber"?
questions.explanation: The Arbeitgeber "gives" work: the employer. The Arbeitnehmer "takes" work: the employee. A job applicant is "der Bewerber".

questions.stem: What is a "befristeter Vertrag"?
questions.explanation: "befristet" means limited to a certain period (die Frist = deadline, time limit). A permanent contract is "unbefristet", part-time is "Teilzeit" and flexitime is "Gleitzeit".

questions.stem: Read the job advert: "Wir suchen ab sofort eine Fachkraft für unser Lager (m/w/d) in Vollzeit. Wir bieten: einen unbefristeten Vertrag, Gleitzeit und regelmäßige Weiterbildung. Sie haben eine abgeschlossene Ausbildung und arbeiten gern im Team. Die Probezeit beträgt sechs Monate. Bitte schicken Sie Ihre Bewerbung bis zum 15. Juni an Frau Kaya." Which is true?
choices: You don't need any training for the job.
The job is permanent and the hours are flexible.
The probationary period is one year.
questions.explanation: The advert offers "einen unbefristeten Vertrag" (permanent) and "Gleitzeit" (flexitime). It is "in Vollzeit" (full-time), asks for "eine abgeschlossene Ausbildung", and the probation is six months.

questions.stem: Which is the correct start of a formal e-mail?
choices: Sehr geehrte Frau Kaya, Mit großem Interesse habe ich Ihre Anzeige gelesen.
Sehr geehrter Frau Kaya, mit großem Interesse habe ich Ihre Anzeige gelesen.
Hallo Frau Kaya! mit großem Interesse habe ich deine Anzeige gelesen.
Sehr geehrte Frau Kaya, mit großem Interesse habe ich Ihre Anzeige gelesen.
questions.explanation: Formal: "Sehr geehrte" for a woman (geehrter for a man), a comma after the name, then a small letter to continue, and Ihre with a capital I. After a comma German doesn't start with a capital, and "deine" is informal.

questions.stem: What does "Der Antrag ist bis Freitag abzugeben." mean?
choices: The application must be handed in by Friday.
The application was handed in on Friday.
The application can't be handed in until Friday.
You don't need to hand in the application.
questions.explanation: "sein + zu + infinitive" has a passive meaning of must or can: it must be handed in (muss abgegeben werden). It is typical of rules and official texts.

questions.stem: Complete: "Nach drei Jahren wurde sie zur Abteilungsleiterin ___."
questions.explanation: "befördern" means to promote: she was promoted to head of department. "entlassen" (to dismiss) and "kündigen" (to quit, give notice) don't fit "zur Abteilungsleiterin", and "sich bewerben" is to apply.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Sie brauchen das Formular nur zu unterschreiben.
Sie brauchen das Formular nur unterschreiben zu.
Sie brauchen zu das Formular nur unterschreiben.
Sie brauchen das Formular nur zu unterschrieben.
questions.explanation: "brauchen nur zu" + infinitive: zu goes directly before the infinitive at the end. "unterschreiben" is inseparable, so zu stays in front (zu unterschreiben), and it takes the infinitive, not the participle.

questions.stem: Which word describes someone who runs their own business?
questions.explanation: "selbstständig" means self-employed. "arbeitslos" is unemployed, "angestellt" means employed by someone else, and "befristet" describes a contract, not a person.

questions.stem: Tom says: "Ich bin krank." Which report is correct?
choices: Tom sagt, dass ich krank bin.
Tom sagt, dass er ist krank.
Tom sagt, ob er krank ist.
Tom sagt, dass er krank ist.
questions.explanation: When you report Tom's words, "ich" becomes "er", and after dass the verb goes to the end: dass er krank ist. "dass ich krank bin" would mean you are ill. "ob" is only for yes/no questions.

questions.stem: Complete: "Die Ärztin fragt, ___ ich Fieber habe."
questions.explanation: A reported yes/no question ("Haben Sie Fieber?") starts with ob (whether, if). English "if" tempts learners to use wenn, but wenn is for conditions and repeated times. dass is for statements, not questions.

questions.stem: The receptionist asks: "Wann haben Sie Zeit?" Which report is correct?
choices: Sie fragt, wann habe ich Zeit.
Sie fragt, wann ich Zeit habe.
Sie fragt, ob wann ich Zeit habe.
Sie fragt, dass ich wann Zeit habe.
questions.explanation: A reported W-question keeps the question word (wann) and puts the verb at the end: wann ich Zeit habe. Keeping question order (wann habe ich) is the typical mistake. Don't add ob or dass to a W-question.

questions.stem: The doctor said: "Nehmen Sie die Tabletten nach dem Essen." Which report is the natural one?
choices: Der Arzt hat gesagt, ich soll die Tabletten nach dem Essen nehmen.
Der Arzt hat gesagt, ich nehme die Tabletten nach dem Essen.
Der Arzt hat gesagt, dass ich die Tabletten nach dem Essen nehmen sollen.
Der Arzt hat gesagt, dass nehmen Sie die Tabletten nach dem Essen.
questions.explanation: Reported instructions use sollen: ich soll … nehmen. "ich nehme" reports a fact, not an instruction. "ich … sollen" has the wrong ending (ich soll), and the last option keeps the original command after dass.

questions.stem: In a news report you read: "Der Minister sagte, das System sei stabil." What does "sei" tell you?
choices: The newspaper is reporting what the minister said, without claiming it is true.
It is a command: Be stable!
It is a spelling mistake for "ist".
It describes something that will happen in the future.
questions.explanation: sei is the Konjunktiv I of sein. News texts use it to show that they are only passing on someone's words: the system is stable, according to the minister. It looks a little like the imperative sei!, but here it has a subject (das System).

questions.stem: Complete the news sentence: "Die Ärzte sagen, sie ___ zu wenig Zeit für ihre Patienten."
questions.explanation: The Konjunktiv I of haben for sie (plural) is haben, which looks exactly like the indicative. So news writers switch to the Konjunktiv II: hätten. habe is only for er/sie/es, and hatten is the simple past.

questions.stem: Your family doctor gives you "eine Überweisung". What is it?
choices: a bank transfer to the doctor
a sick note for your employer
questions.explanation: At the doctor's, eine Überweisung is a referral: it sends you on to a Facharzt or Fachärztin. You know the word from A2 as a bank transfer, but here the meaning is "sent over to someone else". A sick note is a doctor's certificate (die Krankschreibung); a prescription is ein Rezept.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Man kann eine Erkältung mit viel Schlaf vorbeugen.
Man kann einer Erkältung mit viel Schlaf vorbeugen.
Man kann einer Erkältung mit viel Schlaf vorgebeugt.
Man vorbeugt einer Erkältung mit viel Schlaf.
questions.explanation: vorbeugen takes the dative (einer Erkältung) and is separable. After the modal kann, the infinitive goes to the end: vorbeugen. The accusative eine Erkältung is the common mistake; vorgebeugt is the participle, and "man vorbeugt" doesn't separate the prefix.

questions.stem: You wake up with a high fever and can't go to work. What is "die Krankmeldung"?
choices: telling your employer that you are ill and can't work
questions.explanation: Die Krankmeldung is the notification that you are ill, which your employer needs on the first day (colloquially the word is also used for the doctor's note). If you are ill for more than three days, your employer also needs a doctor's certificate: the doctor krankschreibt you (signs you off sick). A referral is eine Überweisung, a prescription ein Rezept.

questions.stem: Which sentence is NOT correct?
choices: Sie sagt, dass sie kommt später.
Sie sagt, dass sie später kommt.
Sie hat gesagt, sie würde später kommen.
questions.explanation: After dass the verb must go to the end: dass sie später kommt. Without dass, main-clause order is fine (Sie sagt, sie kommt später). The Konjunktiv II version is also normal in speech and adds a little distance.

questions.stem: "Was hat die Ärztin gesagt?" Which answer is correct?
choices: Sie hat gesagt, ob ich mich zwei Tage ausruhe.
Sie hat gesagt, ich soll ausruhen mich zwei Tage.
Sie hat gefragt, dass ich mich zwei Tage ausruhen soll.
Sie hat gesagt, dass ich mich zwei Tage ausruhen soll.
questions.explanation: An instruction is reported with dass … sollen, verb at the end, and the reflexive pronoun changes to fit the new speaker (mich). ob is for questions, "gefragt, dass" mixes a question verb with a statement, and "ich soll ausruhen mich" has the wrong word order.

questions.stem: Read: "Laut einer Studie warten Patienten im Durchschnitt sechs Wochen auf einen Termin beim Facharzt. Eine Sprecherin der Ärzte sagte, das Problem sei bekannt. Es gebe aber nicht genug Fachärzte auf dem Land." According to the text, what did the spokeswoman say?
choices: That patients wait six weeks for their family doctor.
That there are not enough specialists in rural areas.
That there are too many specialists in the cities.
questions.explanation: The Konjunktiv I forms sei and gebe report what the spokeswoman said: the problem is known, and there aren't enough specialists auf dem Land (in the countryside). The six weeks are for a Facharzt, not the family doctor, and the problem is bekannt (known), not new.

questions.stem: A letter from a health insurance fund: "Ab diesem Jahr übernehmen wir einmal im Jahr die Kosten für eine professionelle Zahnreinigung. Bitte schicken Sie uns die Rechnung der Zahnarztpraxis per App oder bringen Sie sie zu einer Beratungsstelle. Für Brillen zahlen wir weiterhin einen Zuschuss von 50 Euro, aber nur mit Rezept. Reiseimpfungen bezahlen wir leider nicht." What must you do to get money for a teeth cleaning?
choices: Nothing: the dentist sends the bill.
Send or bring the dentist's bill to the insurance fund.
questions.explanation: The letter says: schicken Sie uns die Rechnung … oder bringen Sie sie zu einer Beratungsstelle. The prescription (Rezept) and the 50 euros belong to the glasses, and travel vaccinations are not paid at all.

questions.stem: You are having your bike repaired. Complete: "Ich ___ mein Fahrrad reparieren."
questions.explanation: To have something done by someone else, German uses lassen + infinitive: Ich lasse mein Fahrrad reparieren. "mache … reparieren" is a translation of a structure German doesn't have, and werde … reparieren would mean that you will repair it yourself.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I'm having my hair cut"?
choices: Ich lasse mir die Haare schneiden.
Ich lasse mir die Haare zu schneiden.
Ich mache mir die Haare schneiden.
questions.explanation: Causative lassen + infinitive, with a dative reflexive pronoun for something done to yourself: Ich lasse mir die Haare schneiden. "Ich schneide mir die Haare" means you cut it yourself. lassen takes no zu.

questions.stem: Complete: "Wir haben die Heizung reparieren ___."
questions.explanation: When lassen is used with another infinitive, its perfect has two infinitives at the end: haben … reparieren lassen, just like modal verbs. gelassen is used only when there is no other verb (Ich habe den Schlüssel im Auto gelassen).

questions.stem: Complete: "Ich habe meinen Schlüssel im Büro ___."
questions.explanation: Here lassen means "to leave" and there is no second infinitive, so the perfect uses the normal participle gelassen. The double-infinitive form (lassen) is only for lassen + another verb.

questions.stem: What does "Das Fenster lässt sich nicht öffnen." mean?
choices: Somebody didn't let me open the window.
questions.explanation: sich lassen + infinitive means that something can (or can't) be done: the window can't be opened. It's common in complaints. It isn't an instruction, and no other person is involved.

questions.stem: What does "Meine Eltern lassen mich allein nach Berlin fahren." mean?
choices: My parents leave me alone in Berlin.
My parents are having me driven to Berlin.
My parents let me go to Berlin alone.
My parents leave Berlin without me.
questions.explanation: lassen + person + infinitive means to let (or make) someone do something. Here the person is mich and the infinitive is fahren: they allow me to travel alone. "leave me alone" would be Sie lassen mich allein, without a second verb.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ du das Auto waschen?" (Are you having the car washed?)
questions.explanation: lassen changes its vowel with du and er/sie/es: du lässt, er lässt, with ss. lasst (no umlaut) is the ihr form, and last and läst are misspellings.

questions.stem: A notice in the hall: "Liebe Mieterinnen und Mieter, am Dienstag, den 14. Mai, lassen wir die Heizungen im ganzen Haus prüfen. Ein Handwerker kommt zwischen 8 und 12 Uhr in jede Wohnung. Wenn Sie nicht zu Hause sein können, geben Sie Ihren Schlüssel bitte bis Montag bei Herrn Kaya im Erdgeschoss ab. Bitte stellen Sie im Treppenhaus keine Kinderwagen oder Fahrräder ab. Ihre Hausverwaltung" What should tenants do if they are at work on Tuesday morning?
choices: Leave their key with Mr Kaya by Monday.
Phone the tradesman to arrange another day.
Move their bikes into the stairwell.
questions.explanation: The notice says: wenn Sie nicht zu Hause sein können, geben Sie Ihren Schlüssel … bei Herrn Kaya ab. The property management is having the heating checked (lassen … prüfen), so tenants don't check it themselves, and bikes must not be left (abstellen) in the stairwell.

questions.stem: A note on the door: "Hallo zusammen, ich ziehe am Samstag um. Kann mir jemand ein paar Umzugskartons ausleihen? Als Dankeschön lade ich alle am Abend zum Grillen in den Hof ein. Viele Grüße, Jonas (3. Stock)" What does Jonas offer his neighbours?
choices: A barbecue in the courtyard in the evening.
questions.explanation: Jonas wants to borrow boxes (Kann mir jemand … ausleihen? = Can someone lend me …?) and invites everyone zum Grillen in den Hof as a thank-you. He is asking for the boxes, not offering them.

questions.stem: What does "Lass uns morgen den Hausmeister anrufen!" mean?
choices: Let the caretaker call us tomorrow!
The caretaker lets us call him tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Lass uns … / Lasst uns … + infinitive is a suggestion, like English "Let's …". The subject who calls is "we" (uns), and den Hausmeister is the person called.

questions.stem: The tap in your kitchen drips. Which message to the property management is correct?
choices: Der Wasserhahn in meiner Küche tropfen. Könnten Sie bitte einen Handwerker schicken?
Mein Wasserhahn tropft mich. Bitte lassen Sie reparieren.
Der Wasserhahn in meiner Küche tropft. Könnten Sie bitte einen Handwerker schicken?
Der Wasserhahn ist undicht gelassen. Schicken Sie bitte lassen.
questions.explanation: Der Wasserhahn tropft (third person singular), followed by a polite Könnten Sie bitte …? The first option has the infinitive tropfen instead of tropft, and the other two are ungrammatical (tropft mich) and misuse lassen without an infinitive.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Ich lasse die Wohnung zu streichen.
questions.explanation: lassen works like a modal verb: bare infinitive (no zu) at the end of the clause. "zu streichen" and the participle gestrichen are wrong here, and the infinitive can't come before the object.

questions.stem: What is a "Mieterverein"?
choices: a tenants' association that advises its members
the company that manages the building
questions.explanation: Der Mieterverein is a tenants' association: for a small yearly fee it advises members on their rights, for example about a Mietminderung. The company that manages a building is die Hausverwaltung; a neighbourhood party is ein Nachbarschaftsfest.

questions.stem: You are inside your flat. Someone knocks at the door. You call: "___!"
questions.explanation: her- marks movement towards the speaker. You are inside, so the visitor comes towards you: Herein! (Come in!). Hinein would be said by someone outside who sends a person in, away from themselves.

questions.stem: You are at the bottom of the stairs and call up to your friend at the top: "Ich komme gleich ___!"
questions.explanation: You move up, away from yourself as the speaker: hinauf. Your friend at the top would say Komm herauf! because for them you move towards them.

questions.stem: What does "Wo kommst du her?" mean?
questions.explanation: Wo … her is the split form of woher: where from. "Where are you going?" is Wo gehst du hin? (wohin). Spoken German often splits the question word like this.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Einerseits das Hotel ist billig, andererseits es liegt weit vom Zentrum.
Einerseits ist das Hotel billig, andererseits es liegt weit vom Zentrum.
Einerseits das Hotel billig ist, andererseits es weit vom Zentrum liegt.
Einerseits ist das Hotel billig, andererseits liegt es weit vom Zentrum.
questions.explanation: einerseits and andererseits take position 1, like deshalb, so the verb comes straight after them: einerseits ist …, andererseits liegt … The other options keep English order or move the verb to the end.

questions.stem: Switzerland is divided into …
questions.explanation: Switzerland has 26 Kantone. Germany (16) and Austria (9) are divided into Bundesländer.

questions.stem: Which sentence fits best at the START of a short presentation?
choices: In meiner Präsentation geht es um die Frage, ob …
questions.explanation: The introduction (Einleitung) names the topic: In meiner Präsentation geht es um … Abschließend and Vielen Dank fürs Zuhören belong to the conclusion, and pros and cons come in the middle.

questions.stem: Which phrase is used to conclude a presentation?
choices: Zuerst erzähle ich von meinen Erfahrungen.
In meinem Heimatland ist das ganz anders.
questions.explanation: abschließend means "to conclude, finally". The others belong to the introduction (Zuerst …, Ich möchte heute über …) or to the part about your home country.

questions.stem: Read: "Das Allgäu im Süden Bayerns ist ein beliebtes Reiseziel. In der Hauptsaison im Juli und August sind viele Hotels voll, und an den Seilbahnen wartet man oft lange. Wer Ruhe sucht, kommt besser im Juni oder im September. Dann sind die Preise niedriger, aber einige Hütten haben schon geschlossen." Which statement is true?
choices: In July and August you hardly wait at the cable cars.
In September prices are lower, but some huts are already closed.
The Allgäu is in the north of Bavaria.
All huts are open in June and September.
questions.explanation: The text says that in June and September die Preise niedriger sind, aber einige Hütten … geschlossen haben. In the high season you wait a long time (lange) at the cable cars, and the Allgäu is im Süden.

questions.stem: What is "die Nebensaison"?
choices: the low season, when fewer tourists come
a second holiday in the same year
questions.explanation: Die Nebensaison is the low season: quieter and cheaper. The high season is die Hauptsaison. Saison is used for tourism, sport and fashion; the four seasons of the year are die Jahreszeiten.

questions.stem: In everyday speech, "Kommst du herein?" is usually shortened to …
questions.explanation: herein and hinein both become rein in speech; heraus/hinaus become raus, herunter/hinunter become runter. "Kommst du hin?" isn't a short form of herein.

questions.stem: What does "die Mundart" mean?
questions.explanation: Die Mundart is a traditional word for dialect (der Dialekt). It is built from der Mund (mouth) and die Art (kind, way), so "way of the mouth", but it simply means a regional way of speaking.

questions.stem: "Was ist ein Vorteil der Nebensaison?" Which answer is correct?
choices: Ein Vorteil ist, weil es billiger ist und ruhig.
Ein Vorteil sind, dass es billiger ist.
Ein Vorteil ist, dass es billiger und ruhiger ist.
Ein Vorteil ist, dass es ist billiger.
questions.explanation: The set phrase is Ein Vorteil ist, dass … with the verb at the end of the dass clause. weil doesn't fit after "Ein Vorteil ist", the verb must agree with Vorteil (ist), and the last option puts the verb in second position after dass.

questions.stem: You are upstairs. Your friend is in the cellar. You ask him to bring a box up to you: "Kannst du die Kiste ___bringen?"
questions.explanation: The box moves up, towards you as the speaker: heraufbringen. Your friend would say "Ich bringe sie hinauf" because from his point of view it moves away from him.

questions.stem: You write to your course teacher, Ms Brandt, whom you know well but call "Sie". Which opening fits best?
questions.explanation: A semi-formal message uses Sie but a friendly opening: Liebe Frau Brandt, with the title Frau. Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren is for companies when you don't know the name, and the surname without Frau is impolite.

questions.stem: Which closing fits a formal complaint to a company?
questions.explanation: Mit freundlichen Grüßen is the standard formal closing. Liebe Grüße and Bis bald are for friends; Tschüss is spoken and informal.

questions.stem: The e-mail begins "Liebe Frau Kraus,". Which next line is correct?
questions.explanation: After the comma of the opening, German starts the next line with a small letter: vielen Dank. The polite Ihre always has a capital (ihre would mean "her"), and Dank is a noun, so it has a capital too.

questions.stem: Which sentence has the comma in the right place?
choices: Ich schreibe Ihnen weil, ich mich nach dem Kurs erkundigen möchte.
Ich schreibe, Ihnen weil ich mich nach dem Kurs erkundigen möchte.
Ich schreibe Ihnen, weil ich mich nach dem Kurs erkundigen möchte.
Ich schreibe Ihnen weil ich mich, nach dem Kurs erkundigen möchte.
questions.explanation: German puts a comma before every subordinate clause, so before weil. The comma never comes after the conjunction or in the middle of the clause.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ich möchte mich ___ den Preisen für den Kurs erkundigen."
questions.explanation: sich erkundigen goes with nach + dative: sich nach den Preisen erkundigen (to ask about the prices). über and für are guesses from English "about" and "for".

questions.stem: A forum post: "Ich finde, dass Vermieter Haustiere grundsätzlich erlauben sollten. Natürlich kann ein Hund laut sein, und manche Nachbarn haben Allergien. Aber für viele ältere Menschen ist ein Haustier der wichtigste Freund. Meine Mutter lebt allein, und seit sie eine Katze hat, ist sie viel glücklicher. Mein Fazit: Regeln ja, Verbote nein." What is the writer's position?
choices: Pets should generally be allowed, with rules.
Pets should be banned because of allergies.
questions.explanation: The writer takes a position in the first sentence (Haustiere grundsätzlich erlauben), mentions the other side (noise, allergies) and ends with a Fazit: rules yes, bans no. Cats are only the personal example.

questions.stem: What does "bzw." stand for?
questions.explanation: bzw. is short for beziehungsweise (or, or rather, respectively): Ich komme am Montag bzw. am Dienstag. sowie (as well as) is another formal linking word that is never abbreviated.

questions.stem: Which sentence is a polite request in a semi-formal e-mail to your teacher?
choices: Sie müssen mir die Hausaufgaben schicken.
Könnten Sie mir bitte die Hausaufgaben schicken?
questions.explanation: Könnten Sie … bitte …? is the key polite form. "Schick mir …" uses du, which is wrong for a teacher you call Sie; "Sie müssen" sounds like an order; and "Hausaufgaben schicken, danke" is not a sentence.

questions.stem: In a complaint you ask for "Ersatz". What do you want?
questions.explanation: Der Ersatz is a replacement (or a substitute): einen kostenlosen Ersatz bekommen. An apology is eine Entschuldigung. Other things you might ask for are a repair, an exchange (der Umtausch) or your money back.

questions.stem: What is wrong with this ending? "Mit freundlichen Grüßen, Anna Weber"
choices: There should be no comma after "Grüßen".
questions.explanation: German puts no punctuation after the closing formula: Mit freundlichen Grüßen, then your name on a new line. The adjective stays lower case, the phrase needs the dative (freundlichen Grüßen), and ß is correct after the long ü.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ich hoffe, ___ Sie mein Anliegen schnell bearbeiten."
questions.explanation: After hoffen, a clause with the verb at the end starts with the conjunction dass. das is an article or pronoun (test: could you say dieses or welches? No). ob is for indirect yes/no questions.

questions.stem: Read: "Liebe Frau Ott, vielen Dank für die Einladung zu Ihrem Gartenfest am Samstag. Leider kann ich nicht kommen, weil meine Schwester an diesem Tag heiratet. Ich hoffe, wir sehen uns bald im Treppenhaus! Viele Grüße, Hanna Berg" Why is Hanna writing?
choices: To invite Ms Ott to a wedding.
To ask about a problem in the stairwell.
questions.explanation: Hanna thanks Ms Ott for the invitation (Einladung) and says leider kann ich nicht kommen, with a reason (weil …). It's a typical semi-formal message: Liebe Frau Ott, Sie, Viele Grüße. The stairwell is only mentioned in a friendly closing sentence.

questions.stem: Which kind of text usually has no "Anrede" and no "Grußformel"?
choices: a semi-formal e-mail to a teacher
an informal e-mail to a friend
questions.explanation: A forum post often starts straight with your opinion, or with a short Hallo zusammen. All kinds of letters and e-mails have an opening (Anrede) and a closing (Grußformel) in the right register.

questions.stem: How long is the reading module (Lesen) of the adult Goethe-Zertifikat B1?
questions.explanation: Lesen takes 65 minutes for five parts. Hören takes about 40 minutes, Schreiben 60 minutes and Sprechen about 15 minutes plus 15 minutes of preparation. 30 minutes was the A2 reading time.

questions.stem: How many points do you need to pass a module of the Goethe-Zertifikat B1?
questions.explanation: Each module is scored out of 100 points and passed with 60. "45 out of 75" was the rule for the written part of the A2 exam.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT one of the B1 writing tasks?
choices: an informal e-mail of about 80 words
a forum post giving your opinion
a semi-formal e-mail of about 40 words
questions.explanation: Schreiben has three tasks: an informal e-mail (about 80 words), a forum post with your opinion (about 80 words) and a semi-formal e-mail (about 40 words). Long essays come at higher levels.

questions.stem: You passed Lesen, Schreiben and Sprechen, but failed Hören. What can you do?
choices: Wait two years before you try again.
questions.explanation: The adult B1 exam is modular: you can take and repeat each module separately. Modules passed within one year can usually be listed on one combined certificate, but check the rules with your exam centre.

questions.stem: You score 74 points in a module. What is your grade?
questions.explanation: The grades: 90–100 sehr gut, 80–89 gut, 70–79 befriedigend, 60–69 ausreichend. 74 falls in the befriedigend band.

questions.stem: What happens in the speaking module (Sprechen)?
choices: In pairs, you plan something together, give a short presentation and react to your partner's.
You talk alone with the examiner about your life for an hour.
You read a text aloud and answer questions on it.
You listen to a dialogue and summarize it.
questions.explanation: Sprechen is taken in pairs: after 15 minutes of preparation you plan something together, each give a short presentation, and react to the partner's presentation and answer questions. It lasts about 15 minutes.

questions.stem: An instruction says: "Ordnen Sie die Anzeigen den Situationen zu." What do you do?
choices: Write an ad for each situation.
Match the ads to the situations.
Put the ads in the right order.
Correct the mistakes in the ads.
questions.explanation: zuordnen means to match or assign: etwas (Akk) einer Sache (Dat) zuordnen. Putting things in order would be in die richtige Reihenfolge bringen.

questions.stem: What does "Trifft das auf Sie zu?" mean?
choices: Are you going to meet them?
questions.explanation: zutreffen auf + accusative means to apply to, to be true of. It's built on treffen, but it has nothing to do with meeting or hitting.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: The passive Präteritum is wurde + participle: wurde gebaut. The Perfekt would be ist … gebaut worden (worden, not geworden, and with sein). The other options mix the two.

questions.stem: Complete: "Je mehr ich lese, ___ besser verstehe ich."
questions.explanation: je + comparative … desto (or umso) + comparative: Je mehr ich lese, desto besser verstehe ich. The je part has the verb at the end; after desto besser the verb comes next.

questions.stem: Complete: "Wenn ich mehr Zeit ___, würde ich öfter reisen."
questions.explanation: An unreal condition uses the Konjunktiv II: Wenn ich mehr Zeit hätte, würde ich … The form hatte (no umlaut) is the simple past and doesn't make the sentence hypothetical.

questions.stem: Complete: "Das ist die Frau, mit ___ ich gesprochen habe."
questions.explanation: mit takes the dative, and die Frau is feminine singular, so the relative pronoun is der. dem is masculine or neuter, denen is plural, and die is nominative or accusative.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Obwohl es regnet, wir gehen spazieren.
Obwohl es regnet, gehen wir spazieren.
Obwohl regnet es, gehen wir spazieren.
Trotzdem es regnet, gehen wir spazieren.
questions.explanation: obwohl starts a subordinate clause (verb at the end), and the whole clause counts as position 1, so the main verb comes next: gehen wir. trotzdem is an adverb, not a conjunction.

questions.stem: Which description fits the CEFR level B1?
choices: You can understand almost everything you hear without effort.
You can only use a few simple phrases about yourself.
You can follow complex technical discussions in any field.
You can describe experiences and plans and briefly give reasons for your opinions.
questions.explanation: B1 users can describe experiences, events, hopes and plans and briefly explain their opinions. Understanding nearly everything is C2, only simple phrases is A1, and technical discussions in your own field are B2.

questions.stem: Which of these is a typical feature of a German Kurzgeschichte?
choices: A long introduction that presents all the characters
A happy ending that answers every question
A story that covers many years
questions.explanation: Kurzgeschichten typically stop without telling us how things end: an open ending (offener Schluss). They start without an introduction, cover a short time (minutes or hours) and rarely tie everything up the way a fairy tale does.

questions.stem: Which features of a Kurzgeschichte does "Der Zettel" show? Select all that apply.
choices: It takes place in one evening.
A narrator explains the father's illness.
It ends without telling us what happens next.
It has many characters from several generations.
questions.explanation: The story begins with "Als Jana aus dem Bus stieg" as if we already knew Jana (sudden start), covers one evening and ends open. The illness is never named: that is a gap the reader fills in. There are only two characters.

questions.stem: Complete the summary in the present tense: "Jana ___ ihren Vater jeden Dienstag." (besuchen)
questions.explanation: An Inhaltsangabe is written in the present tense, even though the story is in the past: Jana besucht ihren Vater. (besuchte would be the simple past of the story itself.)

questions.stem: Which sentence belongs in an Inhaltsangabe of "Der Zettel"?
choices: Jana besuchte ihren Vater jeden Dienstag.
Jana besucht ihren Vater jeden Dienstag.
Ich finde die Geschichte sehr traurig.
questions.explanation: An Inhaltsangabe is in the present tense, has no direct speech and no opinion. The first choice is in the past, the second quotes direct speech, and the last gives an opinion.

questions.stem: Put the events of "Der Zettel" in the order they happen.
choices: Jana findet drei Flaschen Milch im Kühlschrank.
Jana verspricht, schon am Montag zu kommen.
questions.explanation: Jana gets off the bus, her father opens the door, she finds the milk while putting away the shopping, then she reads the note, and at the end she promises to come on Monday.

questions.stem: What is the turning point (der Wendepunkt) of "Der Zettel"?
choices: Jana reads the note on the kitchen table.
Jana gets off the bus in the rain.
The father talks about a football match.
questions.explanation: Before the note, Jana notices small strange things (the milk, the TV that is off). The note shows her what they mean, and right afterwards she hides it and decides to come more often. The bus and the darkness frame the story; the football match shows that his old memories are still clear.

questions.stem: Match each feature of a Kurzgeschichte to its meaning.
choices: Ends without telling how things turn out
The moment that changes the situation
Something important the text leaves unsaid
A long description of the setting
questions.explanation: An unvermittelter Anfang drops us into the action, an offener Schluss leaves the outcome open, the Wendepunkt changes the situation, and a Leerstelle is something important the text leaves unsaid. A long description of the setting is not typical of the form.

questions.stem: "Als ich aus dem Bus stieg, regnete es." What kind of narrator tells this sentence?
questions.explanation: The narrator says ich and is part of the story: a first-person narrator (Ich-Erzähler). That doesn't make it the author; the narrator is a voice inside the text.

questions.stem: Which statement about narrator and author is correct?
choices: The narrator is always the author.
A first-person narrator is always the author.
The narrator is the voice in the text; the author is the real person who wrote it.
questions.explanation: Der Erzähler is the voice that tells the story, der Autor the real person who wrote it. Even an ich in a story is a narrator, not necessarily the author, and every story, long or short, has a narrator.

questions.stem: Rewrite in the present tense for a summary: "Sie faltete den Zettel zusammen." → "Sie ___ den Zettel ___."
questions.explanation: zusammenfalten is separable: in the present, faltet goes to position 2 and zusammen to the end: Sie faltet den Zettel zusammen.

questions.stem: Which is the best introduction sentence for an Inhaltsangabe?
choices: In der Kurzgeschichte „Der Zettel“ geht es um eine junge Frau, die merkt, dass ihr Vater immer vergesslicher wird.
Die Geschichte „Der Zettel“ ist sehr schön und spannend.
In der Geschichte geht es um Milch und einen Zettel.
Jana stieg aus dem Bus, und es regnete.
questions.explanation: The introduction names title, text type and the theme, what the story is really about. The second choice is an opinion, the third names objects instead of the theme, and the fourth retells the first sentence in the past.

questions.stem: What is "Trümmerliteratur" (rubble literature)?
choices: Fairy tales collected by the Brothers Grimm
Literature written soon after 1945 about the war, hunger and ruins
questions.explanation: die Trümmer are the ruins of bombed cities. Writers such as Wolfgang Borchert and Heinrich Böll wrote about the war and its aftermath in plain language, and the German Kurzgeschichte grew out of this.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the short-story tension curve.

image.alt: A tension curve over time with four numbered points on the short-story line: its start halfway up, the rising middle, the peak and the dotted end with a question mark. A grey dashed fairy-tale curve is shown for comparison.

questions.explanation: The short story starts already halfway up (unvermittelter Anfang), rises through the Hauptteil to the Wendepunkt and stops in the air: offener Schluss. A Happy End belongs to the fairy-tale curve, and an Einleitung is exactly what a Kurzgeschichte leaves out.

questions.stem: How should „Hast du gegessen?“, fragte sie. appear in an Inhaltsangabe?
choices: Sie fragt ihn, ob er schon gegessen hat.
Sie fragte ihn, ob er gegessen hatte.
questions.explanation: No direct speech and the present tense: a yes/no question becomes an ob clause with the verb at the end. The third choice uses ob but is in the past; the others keep the quotation.

questions.stem: Im Garten blüht der erste Baum, / der Winter war ein langer Traum. / Die Kinder rennen aus dem Haus, / der Frühling ruft: „Kommt alle raus!“ What is the rhyme scheme?
questions.explanation: Baum rhymes with Traum (a, a) and Haus with raus (b, b): the lines rhyme in pairs, aabb, a Paarreim.

questions.stem: What is the rhyme scheme of the first stanza of Mondnacht (lines ending Himmel, geküsst, Blütenschimmer, müsst')? Type four letters, for example aabb.
questions.explanation: Himmel is a, geküsst is b, Blütenschimmer rhymes (impurely) with Himmel (a), müsst' rhymes with geküsst (b): abab, a Kreuzreim.

questions.stem: Name the three rhyme schemes.

image.alt: Three columns of four lines with rhyme letters: a a b b, a b a b and a b b a, each with a number above it.

questions.explanation: aabb is the Paarreim (pairs), abab the Kreuzreim (the rhymes cross), abba the umarmende Reim (one pair embraces the other). A Strophe is a stanza and a Zeilensprung is enjambment; neither is a rhyme scheme.

questions.stem: Match each old or poetic form from Mondnacht to its everyday German.
questions.explanation: hätt' and leis have lost their final -e, die Lande is an old plural of Land (today die Länder), nach Haus has lost the -e of nach Hause, and flöge is the Konjunktiv II of fliegen, which everyday German replaces with würde fliegen.

questions.stem: In German, "der Vers" means …
questions.explanation: German Vers is one line (also called Zeile). A stanza is die Strophe, which is also the word for a song's verse.

questions.stem: Which of these are old or poetic forms that you should not use in an everyday e-mail? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: hätt' (today hätte), die Lande (today die Länder) and flöge (today usually würde fliegen) sound about 200 years old. zu Hause keeps an old dative -e but is completely normal today, and bald is an ordinary word.

questions.stem: Rewrite Heine's line "Ich weiß nicht, was soll es bedeuten" in everyday word order, with the verb at the end of the was clause.
questions.explanation: An indirect question with was sends the conjugated verb to the end: Ich weiß nicht, was es bedeuten soll. Heine keeps main-clause order for the rhythm.

questions.stem: What is enjambment (der Zeilensprung)?
choices: A sentence that runs on from one line into the next
A line with an old dative -e
questions.explanation: In Und meine Seele spannte / Weit ihre Flügel aus, the sentence doesn't stop at the end of the line: that is enjambment. Dropping a final -e is elision.

questions.stem: In Mondnacht, the earth (die Erde) dreams "von ihm". Who or what is "ihm"?
questions.explanation: ihm is masculine (or neuter) dative, and the poem has just said that der Himmel kissed die Erde. So she, the earth, dreams of him, the sky. Nacht and Seele are feminine, and der Wald is not in the first stanza.

questions.stem: Heine calls the Loreley story "ein Märchen aus alten Zeiten". What is surprising about that?
choices: The Brothers Grimm collected it in 1819.
Clemens Brentano had invented it in 1801, only about 20 years earlier.
questions.explanation: The Loreley legend is not an old folk tale: Clemens Brentano made it up in a ballad of 1801. Heine wrote his poem in 1824, so the "tale from olden times" was quite new.

questions.stem: Write the line in today's spelling: Heine wrote "Daß ich so traurig bin". Today: "___ ich so traurig bin."
questions.explanation: Since the 1996 spelling reform, daß is written dass (ß after a short vowel became ss).

questions.stem: Complete: "Ich habe das Gedicht ___ gelernt." (I learned the poem by heart.)
questions.explanation: auswendig lernen means to learn by heart. herzlich means warm, cordial (herzliche Grüße), not "by heart".

questions.stem: What is the rhyme scheme of the whole of Mondnacht (Himmel, geküsst, Blütenschimmer, müsst' / Felder, sacht, Wälder, Nacht / spannte, aus, Lande, Haus)?
questions.explanation: Each stanza has alternate rhyme with new sounds: Himmel/Blütenschimmer and geküsst/müsst' (abab), Felder/Wälder and sacht/Nacht (cdcd), spannte/Lande and aus/Haus (efef). abab abab abab would need the same rhyme sounds in every stanza.

questions.stem: Which pair of rhyme words from Mondnacht is an impure rhyme (unreiner Reim)?
questions.explanation: Himmel and Schimmer share the stressed i and the mm but end differently (-el, -er): close, not identical. sacht/Nacht, aus/Haus and geküsst/müsst' rhyme perfectly from the stressed vowel on.

questions.stem: Why is 9 November called "der Schicksalstag" (the day of fate)?
choices: Because the Berlin Wall was built on that day
Because several turning points of German history happened on that date
Because it is the German national holiday
Because the Second World War ended on that day
questions.explanation: 1918 (the republic is proclaimed), 1923 (Hitler's failed putsch), 1938 (the November pogroms) and 1989 (the fall of the Wall) all happened on 9 November. The Wall was built in 1961, the national holiday is 3 October and the war in Europe ended on 8 May 1945.

questions.stem: Match each 9 November to what happened.
choices: A republic is proclaimed in Berlin
questions.explanation: 1918: the republic is proclaimed; 1923: Hitler's failed putsch in Munich; 1938: the November pogroms; 1989: the Berlin Wall falls. Reunification came on 3 October 1990.

questions.stem: Rewrite the Stolperstein line "DEPORTIERT 1942" as a full sentence about Rosa Adler: "Sie ___ 1942 deportiert."
questions.explanation: Rosa Adler didn't deport anyone; she was deported. So the participle stands for a passive in the past: Sie wurde 1942 deportiert.

questions.stem: What does "JG. 1903" on a Stolperstein mean?
questions.explanation: JG. is short for Jahrgang, the year someone was born: Sie wurde 1903 geboren.

questions.stem: Which statements about Stolpersteine are true? Select all that apply.
choices: Each stone carries the name of one person.
They are placed in front of the person's last freely chosen home.
They are paid for by the federal government.
Every German city allows them on public ground.
The artist Gunter Demnig laid the first one in 1992.
questions.explanation: Each stone remembers one person, in front of the last home they chose freely. Neighbours, school classes, relatives and local groups pay for them, not the federal government, and Munich, for example, doesn't allow them on public ground. Demnig laid the first one in Cologne in 1992.

questions.stem: Complete: "Wir gedenken ___ Opfer."
questions.explanation: gedenken takes the genitive, and the genitive plural article is der: Wir gedenken der Opfer. In everyday German: Wir erinnern an die Opfer.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the picture.

image.alt: A house front with a door, a pavement with a small brass stone, and a magnified view of the stone's text with four numbered points.

questions.explanation: 1 is the front door, 2 the pavement, 3 the brass stone set into it, and 4 the line JG. 1903, the year of birth (Jahrgang). The name is the line ROSA ADLER, which has no number.

questions.stem: What is special about a "Mahnmal"?
choices: It is a museum about art.
It warns: it remembers a crime so that it never happens again.
questions.explanation: Mahnmal comes from mahnen, to warn. A Denkmal can also honour a person or a victory; a cemetery is der Friedhof.

questions.stem: Put the events from the plaque in time order.
choices: Die Druckerei wird von SA-Männern zerstört.
Paul kommt mit einem Kindertransport nach England.
Rosa und Max Adler werden deportiert.
Die Bürger der Stadt hängen die Gedenktafel auf.
questions.explanation: 1938: the printing works is destroyed; 1939: Paul reaches England with a Kindertransport; 1942: Rosa and Max are deported; 2008: the citizens put up the plaque.

questions.stem: "Rosa Adler deportierte 1942." What is wrong with this sentence?
choices: The active voice says she deported someone; it must be passive: Rosa Adler wurde 1942 deportiert.
deportieren is a strong verb, so the past is deportiert.
questions.explanation: Things were done to the victims, so memorial texts use the passive: wurde … deportiert. deportieren is a regular -ieren verb (deportierte, hat deportiert); the problem is the meaning, not the form.

questions.stem: What does "Vergangenheitsbewältigung" mean?
choices: coming to terms with the past
questions.explanation: die Vergangenheit (the past) + die Bewältigung (coping with, mastering). Many people prefer die Aufarbeitung (working through).

questions.stem: Which sentence means "The plaque commemorates the Adler family"?
choices: Die Tafel erinnert sich an die Familie Adler.
Die Tafel gedenkt die Familie Adler.
Die Tafel erinnert der Familie Adler.
Die Tafel erinnert an die Familie Adler.
questions.explanation: erinnern an + accusative without sich means to remind of or commemorate. sich erinnern an means to remember (a plaque can't remember), and gedenken would need the genitive: der Familie Adler.

questions.stem: A Stolperstein says: HIER WOHNTE PAUL ADLER … FLUCHT 1939 / ENGLAND. Complete with the simple past of fliehen: "1939 ___ er nach England."
questions.explanation: fliehen is strong (ie – o – o): floh, ist geflohen. Here the verb is active, because Paul acted himself: 1939 floh er nach England.
