questions.stem: Why do memorial texts use so many passive sentences?
choices: Because they are about things that were done to people
Because German has no active voice in the past
Because plaques must be in the future tense
questions.explanation: The victims are the subject of the text, and what happened was done to them by others: wurde zerstört, wurden deportiert. The passive puts them in first place.

questions.stem: With which country did West Germany sign its first recruitment agreement, in 1955?
questions.explanation: The first Anwerbeabkommen was signed with Italy in December 1955. Spain and Greece followed in 1960, Turkey in 1961.

questions.stem: Put the recruitment agreements in time order.
questions.explanation: Italy 1955, Turkey 1961, Morocco 1963, Yugoslavia 1968.

questions.stem: What happened after the recruitment stop (Anwerbestopp) of 1973?
choices: Many workers stayed and brought their families.
Guest workers had to become German citizens.
questions.explanation: Leaving now meant never being able to come back, so many workers stayed and their families joined them. Temporary workers became immigrants.

questions.stem: The share rose from 20 % to 24 %. By how many percentage points did it rise? Give only the number.
questions.explanation: Percentage points are the plain difference: 24 − 20 = 4.

questions.stem: The share rose from 20 % to 24 %. By how many per cent did it rise compared with the old value? Give only the number.
questions.explanation: Compare the difference with the old value: 4 ÷ 20 = 0.2, so it rose by 20 per cent (and by 4 percentage points).

questions.stem: The share ended at 24 %. Which sentence says that correctly?
choices: Der Anteil hat auf 24 Prozent gestiegen.
Der Anteil ist auf 24 Prozent gestiegen.
questions.explanation: auf gives the new value, um the difference. steigen takes sein in the perfect, and Prozent has no plural ending after a number.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the chart.

image.alt: A bar chart of the share of residents with an immigration history in Neustadt, 2000 to 2024, with four numbered points.

questions.explanation: 1 is the title, 2 one of the bars (die Säule; this kind of chart is a Säulendiagramm), 3 the vertical axis with the percentages, and 4 the source line, Quelle. The chart has no legend, and it isn't a pie chart (Kreisdiagramm).

questions.stem: Match each verb to its meaning in a chart description.
questions.explanation: steigen = to rise, sinken = to fall, gleich bleiben = to stay the same, sich verdoppeln = to double. "To halve" would be sich halbieren.

questions.stem: Which statements about the Neustadt chart (12 %, 15 %, 20 %, 24 %) are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: The biggest rise was between 2008 and 2016.
In 2024 about one in four residents had an immigration history.
questions.explanation: 12 → 24 is a doubling. The rises are 3, 5 and 4 points, so 2008–2016 is the biggest. 24 % is about a quarter. The share rose, not fell, from 2016 to 2024, and the chart says the numbers are invented.

questions.stem: Which statement is correct?
choices: Ausländer are people without German citizenship; many were born in Germany.
Einwanderungsgeschichte means having one grandparent born abroad.
Migrationshintergrund and Ausländer mean the same.
questions.explanation: Ausländer only means "without German citizenship". Many immigrants have become German, and many Ausländer were born in Germany. Einwanderungsgeschichte means you or both your parents immigrated since 1950.

questions.stem: Max Frisch wrote in 1965: „Man hat Arbeitskräfte gerufen, und es kommen Menschen.“ What did he mean?
choices: The workers were people with families and lives, not just labour that would leave again.
questions.explanation: Arbeitskräfte (workers, labour) were what the countries wanted; Menschen (people) are what arrived, with families, needs and lives of their own.

questions.stem: Complete: "Der Anteil ___ in den letzten Jahren gestiegen."
questions.explanation: steigen is a verb of change of state and takes sein in the perfect: Der Anteil ist gestiegen. The same goes for sinken: ist gesunken.

questions.stem: Since the 2024 reform, after how many years of residence can people usually be naturalised in Germany?
questions.explanation: The 2024 reform lowered the usual period from eight to five years. A three-year fast track was added at the same time but abolished again in 2025.

questions.stem: Which is correct?
questions.explanation: After a number, Prozent has no plural ending: 25 Prozent. With a plural noun after it, the verb is usually plural: 25 Prozent der Einwohner haben …

questions.stem: Write the simple past (er/sie form) of each verb: schreiben → ___, bringen → ___, arbeiten → ___.
questions.explanation: schreiben is strong (ei – ie – ie): schrieb, with no ending in the er form. bringen is mixed: new vowel and -te, brachte. arbeiten is weak, and its stem ends in -t, so it adds -ete: arbeitete.

questions.stem: Match each verb to its type.
questions.explanation: finden – fand and schreiben – schrieb change the vowel and add no -te: strong. sagen – sagte and entdecken – entdeckte keep the vowel and add -te: weak. denken – dachte and kennen – kannte do both: mixed.

questions.stem: Which simple past forms are correct? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: er fand, ich schrieb and wir dachten are correct. Strong verbs never add -te (sie ging, not gingte), and the ich and er forms have no ending (er kam, not kame).

questions.stem: The sentence is "Plötzlich rief der Zeuge die Polizei an." Name the numbered parts.

image.alt: The sentence Plötzlich rief der Zeuge die Polizei an split into five boxes. A bracket joins rief and an. Four boxes are numbered: rief, der Zeuge, die Polizei and an.

questions.explanation: anrufen is separable. In a main clause the past form rief stands in position 2 and the prefix an goes to the end, framing the sentence. der Zeuge (nominative) is the subject, die Polizei the object. There is no participle or infinitive in a simple past sentence.

questions.stem: Put the words in order to say "Then the witness phoned the police." Start with "Dann".
questions.explanation: After Dann in position 1, the verb comes next: rief. Then the subject der Zeuge, the object die Polizei, and the separable prefix an at the very end.

questions.stem: Complete with the past perfect of "abfahren": "Als wir am Bahnhof ankamen, ___ der Zug schon ___."
questions.explanation: The train left before we arrived, so it needs the past perfect. abfahren takes sein in the perfect (ist abgefahren), so the past perfect is war … abgefahren.

questions.stem: A written story is set in 1961. Name the tense you would use for each numbered point: 1 Die Tante ___ (fliehen, shortly before), 2 Die Regierung ___ die Mauer (bauen), 3 Berlin ___ wieder eine Stadt (today).

image.alt: A timeline with three numbered points: 1961 shortly before, 1961, and heute. A dashed arrow looks back from the second point to the first.

questions.explanation: The story is told in the simple past (Die Regierung baute die Mauer). Something that happened before the story's time steps back into the past perfect (Die Tante war geflohen). Today's situation is in the present (Berlin ist wieder eine Stadt).

questions.stem: Match each word to the kind of word it is.
questions.explanation: nachdem and bevor start a clause with the verb at the end (nachdem der Krieg zu Ende war). nach and vor are followed by a noun in the dative (nach dem Krieg). danach and vorher stand in a main clause and the verb follows directly (Danach ging er nach Hause).

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct written German? Select all that apply.
choices: Nachdem er gegessen hatte, ging er spazieren.
Nachdem er aß, ging er spazieren.
Nach dem Essen ging er spazieren.
Bevor er ging, aß er etwas.
questions.explanation: A nachdem clause goes one step further back than the main clause: gegessen hatte, not aß. Nach dem Essen is a preposition with a noun, which is fine. After the adverb danach the verb comes straight away (Danach ging er spazieren). bevor takes the same tense as the main clause, so Bevor er ging, aß er etwas is correct.

questions.stem: Put these events from the text "Ein Zeitzeuge erzählt" in the order they happened.
choices: Die Tante floh mit ihren Kindern in den Westen.
Die Regierung der DDR baute die Mauer.
questions.explanation: The aunt had fled shortly before the Wall was built in 1961 (war kurz zuvor geflohen). Herr Brandt, born in 1958, finished school after that and became an electrician. The border opened on 9 November 1989, and he lost his job in 1991.

questions.stem: Each picture shows a time clause (pink) and a main clause (blue). Which conjunction does each picture show?

image.alt: Four numbered timelines. 1: a shorter pink bar lies under a longer blue bar at the same time. 2: a pink dot marks a start, and a blue bar runs from it to a line marked jetzt. 3: a blue bar ends exactly at a pink dot. 4: a pink dot is followed immediately by a blue bar.

questions.explanation: 1 während: both things happen at the same time. 2 seit: the main clause starts at the event and continues until now. 3 bis: the main clause stops at the event. 4 sobald: the main clause starts immediately after the event. weil and dass are not time conjunctions.

questions.stem: Complete with "als" or "wenn": "___ ich klein war, wohnten wir in Kiel. ___ wir Oma besuchten, gab es immer Kuchen."
questions.explanation: Childhood is one period in the past, so als. The visits happened again and again (you could add jedes Mal), so wenn.

questions.stem: Which sentences have the correct word order? Select all that apply.
choices: Während ich im Büro bin, kocht meine Mutter.
Seit sie in Rente ist, reist sie viel.
Bis wir finden eine Wohnung, wohnen wir hier.
questions.explanation: In a time clause the verb goes to the end (im Büro bin, in Rente ist), and when the time clause comes first, the main clause starts with its verb (kocht meine Mutter, reist sie). Correct would be: Sobald er kommt, essen wir. Bis wir eine Wohnung finden, wohnen wir hier.

questions.stem: Match each conjunction to its meaning.
questions.explanation: während = while (also whereas), seit/seitdem = since, bis = until, sobald = as soon as, solange = as long as. "Although" is obwohl, which comes in module 2.

questions.stem: Put the words in order to say "As soon as the children are asleep, I'll call you." Start with "Sobald".
questions.explanation: In the sobald clause the verb schlafen goes to the end. The main clause then starts with its verb (rufe), followed by the subject ich, the object dich and the separable prefix an.

questions.stem: Write the correct form of werden: "Du ___ das schaffen." "Es ___ bald regnen."
questions.explanation: werden is irregular: du wirst (no d) and er/sie/es wird. The infinitive (schaffen, regnen) goes to the end.

questions.stem: Match each sentence to the job "werden" does in it.
questions.explanation: werden + noun or adjective means to become. werden + infinitive is the future, or, with wohl and a present situation, a guess about now. werden + past participle (gebaut) is the passive.

questions.stem: In which situations is werden + infinitive the most natural choice? Select all that apply.
choices: A weather forecast saying that rain is coming.
A promise to a friend that you will help.
Telling a friend your plan to go to Hamburg tomorrow.
Saying that the meeting starts at ten.
questions.explanation: Predictions and promises use werden: Es wird regnen. Ich werde dir helfen. Plans with a time word and timetables are normally in the present: Morgen fahre ich nach Hamburg. Das Meeting beginnt um zehn.

questions.stem: Put the words in order to say "I believe that technology will change our lives." Start with "Ich".
questions.explanation: dass sends the verb to the end. In the future, werden is the conjugated verb, so it comes last of all, after the infinitive: … dass die Technik unser Leben verändern wird.

questions.stem: Say it as a guess with werden + wohl: "Er ist wahrscheinlich im Labor." → "Er ___ wohl im Labor ___."
questions.explanation: werden + wohl + infinitive makes an assumption about the present: Er wird wohl im Labor sein (he's probably in the lab). Nothing here is about the future.

questions.stem: Complete with the correct form: "Ich frage meinen ___ (Kollege)." "Wir sprechen mit dem ___ (Nachbar)."
questions.explanation: Both are weak nouns: they add -n in every form except the nominative singular. Accusative: meinen Kollegen. Dative: dem Nachbarn.

questions.stem: Which nouns are weak nouns (n-declension)? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: der Student and der Präsident are foreign words for people in -ent; der Junge is a masculine person ending in -e. der Tisch is a normal noun (den Tisch), and feminine nouns like die Kollegin are never weak.

questions.stem: Complete each sentence with the right form of "Deutsche/Deutscher".
questions.explanation: Deutsche is an adjectival noun, so it takes adjective endings: ein Deutscher (masculine after ein), eine Deutsche, die Deutschen (plural after die), mit einem Deutschen (dative). Deutsch with no ending is the language.

questions.stem: Put the words in order to say "Yesterday I helped the Frenchman." Start with "Gestern".
questions.explanation: helfen takes the dative, and der Franzose is a weak noun: dem Franzosen. The perfect follows the bracket: habe in position 2, geholfen at the end.

questions.stem: Complete: "Gibt es etwas ___ (neu)?" "Alles ___ (gut) zum Geburtstag!"
questions.explanation: Adjectives used as nouns for things are written with a capital letter. After etwas the ending is -es (etwas Neues); after alles it is -e (alles Gute).

questions.stem: Which sentence is in the Futur II?
choices: Er wird den Brief geschrieben haben.
questions.explanation: The Futur II is werden + participle + haben/sein: wird … geschrieben haben. "wird … schreiben" is the Futur I, "hatte … geschrieben" the past perfect, and "wird … geschrieben" without haben is incomplete.

questions.stem: Complete with "ankommen": "Morgen um diese Zeit ___ sie schon in Rom ___."
questions.explanation: ankommen takes sein in the perfect (sie ist angekommen), so the Futur II is wird … angekommen sein. The helper is always the same as in the perfect, and the participle (angekommen), not the infinitive, is needed.

questions.stem: "Sie antwortet nicht. Sie wird die Nachricht nicht gesehen haben." What does the second sentence mean?
choices: She will have to see the message.
She probably hasn't seen the message.
questions.explanation: With no future time point, the Futur II is a guess about the past: she probably hasn't seen it. "won't see" would be Futur I (wird … nicht sehen), and "hadn't seen" is the past perfect (hatte … gesehen).

questions.stem: Which is the most natural everyday way to say "By Friday I'll have written the report"?
choices: Bis Freitag hatte ich den Bericht geschrieben.
Bis Freitag habe ich den Bericht geschrieben.
Bis Freitag werde ich den Bericht geschrieben.
Bis Freitag wird der Bericht schreiben.
questions.explanation: In speech, the perfect plus a time word usually replaces the Futur II: Bis Freitag habe ich den Bericht geschrieben. "hatte … geschrieben" is the past perfect, "werde … geschrieben" lacks haben, and "wird der Bericht schreiben" says the report will write.

questions.stem: Which subordinate clause is correct?
choices: …, dass er wird den Zug verpasst haben.
…, dass er den Zug haben verpasst wird.
…, dass er den Zug verpasst haben wird.
…, dass er den Zug verpasst wird haben.
questions.explanation: In a subordinate clause the conjugated verb goes to the very end. In the Futur II that is werden, after the perfect infinitive: … verpasst haben wird.

questions.stem: "Wo ist Lisa?" — "Sie ___ wohl noch im Büro ___." (She's probably still at the office.)
questions.explanation: The guess is about now, so it is the Futur I + wohl: Sie wird wohl noch im Büro sein. "wird … gewesen sein" (Futur II) would be a guess about the past: she was probably at the office.

questions.stem: "Gestern war er nicht beim Training. Er wird krank gewesen sein." What does the speaker think?
choices: He is going to become ill.
questions.explanation: The Futur II here is a guess about the past: er wird krank gewesen sein = he was probably ill. It is a supposition, not a certainty and not a statement about the future.

questions.stem: In the text "Der Einbruch in der Bäckerei", why does Kommissarin Yilmaz think the culprit knew the bakery well?
choices: He left fingerprints on the till.
He didn't touch the safe, because he knew there was no money in it.
He came in through the front door with a key.
The baker saw him in the night.
questions.explanation: "Der Täter hat nur die Kasse geöffnet und den Tresor nicht angefasst. Er wird gewusst haben, dass dort kein Geld war." Only an insider would know that. There were no fingerprints, and he came in through the window.

questions.stem: Put "Wir befragen alle Zeugen." into the Futur II: "Bis heute Abend ___ wir alle Zeugen ___ ___."
questions.explanation: werden in position 2, then the perfect infinitive at the end: befragt haben (befragen is inseparable, so no ge-, and it takes haben). Bis heute Abend werden wir alle Zeugen befragt haben.

questions.stem: Make a guess about the past with "einsteigen": "Das Fenster ist offen. Der Täter ___ durch das Fenster ___ ___."
questions.explanation: einsteigen is separable and takes sein (ist eingestiegen), so the Futur II is wird … eingestiegen sein: the culprit probably climbed in through the window.

questions.stem: Put the words in order to say "By then we will have found the culprit." Start with "Bis dahin".
questions.explanation: Bis dahin fills position 1, so werden comes next, then the subject wir. The perfect infinitive gefunden haben closes the sentence.

questions.stem: Match each sentence to its meaning.
left: Er wird wohl krank gewesen sein.
Bis Montag wird er das Buch gelesen haben.
Er wird das Buch morgen lesen.
choices: By Monday he will have read the book.
He is going to read the book tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Futur I + wohl guesses about now; Futur II + wohl guesses about the past. With a future point (bis Montag) the Futur II says what will be finished by then. Futur I with a time word is a plan or prediction. "He had read the book" would be the past perfect: Er hatte das Buch gelesen.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct Futur II? Select all that apply.
choices: Wir werden das Haus verkauft haben.
Ich werde den Film gesehen sein.
Ihr werdet es bis dahin geschafft haben.
questions.explanation: The helper is the same as in the perfect: sie ist gegangen → wird gegangen sein; wir haben verkauft → werden verkauft haben; ihr habt geschafft → werdet geschafft haben. gehen takes sein, not haben, and sehen takes haben, not sein.

questions.stem: The timeline has two reference points, damals in the past and Freitag in the future. Name the tense at each numbered point.

image.alt: A timeline with jetzt in the middle, a reference point damals in the past and a reference point Freitag in the future. Five points are numbered from left to right: one before damals, damals itself, jetzt, one just before Freitag, and Freitag itself. Arrows look back from damals to point 1 and from Freitag to point 4.

questions.explanation: The past perfect looks back from a past point (damals) to something earlier; the Futur II looks back from a future point (Freitag) to something finished before it. damals itself is told in the simple past or perfect, jetzt in the present, and Freitag in the Futur I. The Konjunktiv II is not a tense on the timeline but a mood for unreal situations.

questions.stem: What does "Die Polizei hat den Einbrecher am Bahnhof festgenommen." mean?
choices: The police held the burglar's hand at the station.
The police released the burglar at the station.
The police arrested the burglar at the station.
The police followed the burglar to the station.
questions.explanation: festnehmen (nahm fest, hat festgenommen) means to arrest. Releasing someone would be freilassen; following would be verfolgen.

questions.stem: Which phrase means the same as "Nachdem sie zurückgekehrt war, …"?
questions.explanation: nachdem + clause becomes nach + dative: nach ihrer Rückkehr. nachdem is a conjunction and cannot stand before a noun. vor means before and seit means since, which change the meaning.

questions.stem: Which phrase can replace the clause in "Als wir ankamen, regnete es."?
questions.explanation: als (and wenn) become bei + dative: bei unserer Ankunft = when we arrived. nach would mean after, seit since and vor before.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ Lesen schläft mein Vater oft ein." (while reading)
questions.explanation: "While doing something" is beim + nominalised infinitive: beim Lesen (bei dem → beim, because das Lesen is neuter). Zum Lesen means for reading (Ich brauche eine Brille zum Lesen).

questions.stem: Which clause means the same as "Nach dem Essen gingen wir spazieren."?
choices: Nachdem wir aßen, gingen wir spazieren.
Nachdem wir gegessen hatten, wir gingen spazieren.
Nachdem wir gegessen hatten, gingen wir spazieren.
Nach wir gegessen hatten, gingen wir spazieren.
questions.explanation: A phrase has no tense, so you choose it: the main clause is in the simple past, and nachdem goes one step further back, into the past perfect. After the clause the main clause starts with its verb (gingen wir). nach cannot introduce a clause.

questions.stem: What is the noun that belongs to "beginnen"?
questions.explanation: beginnen has a short stem noun: der Beginn (vor Beginn des Konzerts). Not every verb makes an -ung noun; you learn these nouns one by one.

questions.stem: According to the plaque, what did Clara Brenner do in 1919?

image.alt: A museum plaque. Clara Brenner (1891–1974), Fotografin. 1891 Geburt in Lübeck. 1910 nach dem Abitur Ausbildung in einem Fotoatelier. 1919 Gründung eines eigenen Ateliers in Hamburg. 1933–1949 Aufenthalt in New York. 1949 nach ihrer Rückkehr Fotos vom Wiederaufbau. 1960 Beginn des Ruhestands, Umzug an die Ostsee. 1974 Tod in Travemünde.

choices: She moved to the Baltic coast.
She founded her own studio in Hamburg.
questions.explanation: "1919 Gründung eines eigenen Ateliers in Hamburg": die Gründung is the noun of gründen (to found). The apprenticeship began in 1910, she returned in 1949 and moved to the Baltic in 1960.

questions.stem: What does "Er war kaum zu Hause, als das Telefon klingelte." mean?
choices: He had hardly got home when the phone rang.
He was rarely at home when the phone rang.
The phone rang because he was at home.
The phone rang before he got home.
questions.explanation: kaum …, als = hardly … when: the phone rang right after he got home. kaum means hardly or barely here, not rarely.

questions.stem: "Sooft ich sie besuche, backt sie einen Kuchen." What does "sooft" mean here?
questions.explanation: sooft (one word) is a conjunction meaning whenever, every time that. As soon as is sobald; so oft as two words means so often.

questions.stem: Write the prepositions: "Seit sie geheiratet haben" → "___ ihrer Heirat"; "Bis er in Rente ging" → "___ ___ seinem Ruhestand".
questions.explanation: seit stays seit (+ dative): seit ihrer Heirat. bis + clause becomes bis zu + dative: bis zu seinem Ruhestand (or bis zum Ruhestand).

questions.stem: Write the noun with its article (nominative): ankommen → ___, gründen → ___, sterben → ___.
questions.explanation: ankommen → die Ankunft (a short stem noun with a vowel change); gründen → die Gründung (-ung nouns are always feminine); sterben → der Tod (a different word altogether).

questions.stem: Match each conjunction to the preposition that replaces it in a time phrase.
questions.explanation: als/wenn → bei, nachdem → nach, bevor → vor, seit → seit, bis → bis zu. wegen (because of) is a preposition of cause, not of time.

questions.stem: Put the words in order to say "After her return she founded a studio." Start with "Nach".
questions.explanation: The phrase nach ihrer Rückkehr fills position 1, so the verb gründete follows, then the subject sie and the object ein Atelier.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Nachdem dem Abitur machte sie eine Ausbildung.
Nach dem Abitur machte sie eine Ausbildung.
Beim Autofahren soll man nicht telefonieren.
Seit ihrer Heirat wohnen sie in Graz.
questions.explanation: Prepositions go with nouns (nach dem Abitur, beim Autofahren, seit ihrer Heirat); conjunctions go with clauses. "Nachdem dem Abitur" puts a conjunction before a noun, and "Bei wir ankamen" puts a preposition before a clause (Als wir ankamen or Bei unserer Ankunft).

questions.stem: Rewrite with nachdem: "Nach der Abfahrt des Zuges rief ich meine Mutter an." → "Nachdem der Zug ___ ___, rief ich meine Mutter an."
questions.explanation: The main clause is in the simple past, so the nachdem clause takes the past perfect. abfahren goes with sein, and in a subordinate clause the conjugated helper is last: nachdem der Zug abgefahren war.

questions.stem: In which sentence does "vor" mean "ago"?
choices: Vor der Abfahrt kontrollierte der Fahrer die Reifen.
Vor dem Konzert aßen wir etwas.
Sie ist vor zwei Jahren umgezogen.
questions.explanation: vor + a time span (vor zwei Jahren) means ago. vor der Abfahrt and vor dem Konzert mean before an event, and vor dem Kino is a place: in front of the cinema.

questions.stem: Complete with obwohl or trotzdem: "Das Kleid war teuer. ___ habe ich es gekauft." and "Ich habe es gekauft, ___ es teuer war."
questions.explanation: The first blank starts a new sentence and is followed straight away by the verb "habe", so it needs the linking adverb: Trotzdem (or the formal Dennoch). The second blank introduces the fact and the verb "war" is at the end, so it needs the conjunction obwohl. Both express the same logic: the price should have stopped the purchase, but it didn't.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "Although Lena earns little, she saves every month." The capitalised word comes first.
questions.explanation: Obwohl Lena wenig verdient, spart sie jeden Monat. After obwohl the conjugated verb "verdient" goes to the end of its clause. The whole obwohl clause then fills position 1, so the main verb "spart" comes straight after the comma, followed by the subject "sie".

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Ich kaufe das Handy, obwohl es teuer ist.
Es ist teuer. Trotzdem ich kaufe es.
Das Handy ist zwar teuer, aber es ist sehr gut.
Trotzdem es teuer ist, kaufe ich es.
Obwohl es teuer ist, kaufe ich es.
questions.explanation: obwohl sends the verb to the end ("obwohl es teuer ist"), and a fronted obwohl clause is followed by the main verb ("kaufe ich"). zwar … aber is correct as written. trotzdem is an adverb, not a conjunction: it needs the verb straight after it ("Trotzdem kaufe ich es"), and it can't introduce a clause like obwohl ("Trotzdem es teuer ist" is wrong).

questions.stem: Both sentences mean "The pay is low, but she likes working there all the same." What job does each numbered box do?

image.alt: Two sentences cut into word boxes. Sentence A: Sie arbeitet gern dort, / obwohl / der Lohn / niedrig / ist. Sentence B: Der Lohn ist niedrig. / Trotzdem / arbeitet / sie / gern dort. Five boxes have numbers below them.

questions.explanation: 1 obwohl is a subordinating conjunction, so 2 the conjugated verb "ist" goes to the end of its clause. In sentence B, 3 Trotzdem is a linking adverb in position 1, so 4 the verb "arbeitet" follows straight after it and 5 the subject "sie" comes after the verb. Neither sentence has a position-0 conjunction like aber or an infinitive with zu.

questions.stem: Match each German phrase to its meaning.
questions.explanation: sich etwas leisten (with a dative pronoun: Ich kann mir das nicht leisten) = to afford; auf etwas verzichten = to do without; Geld ausgeben = to spend money; Schulden machen = to get into debt; Das lohnt sich = it's worth it. To save money is sparen, and spending time is Zeit verbringen, not ausgeben.

questions.stem: Complete with um, damit or ohne: "Ich lerne Deutsch, ___ in Wien zu arbeiten." / "Ich erkläre es noch einmal, ___ du es verstehst." / "Er ist einfach gegangen, ___ sich zu verabschieden."
questions.explanation: 1: same subject (I learn, I work) and zu + infinitive at the end: um … zu. 2: different subjects (I explain, you understand) and a full clause with the verb at the end: damit. 3: he simply left without saying goodbye: ohne … zu, which works like um … zu.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "To get a scholarship, you need good grades." The capitalised word comes first.
questions.explanation: Um ein Stipendium zu bekommen, braucht man gute Noten. um starts the clause and zu + infinitive ends it. The whole um … zu clause fills position 1, so the main verb "braucht" comes straight after the comma, then the subject "man".

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Meine Eltern sparen, um ich studieren kann.
Ich spare, um ein Auto zu kaufen.
Sie geht in die Bibliothek, um in Ruhe zu lernen.
Der Lehrer spricht langsam, um wir ihn verstehen.
Wir fahren früh los, um pünktlich anzukommen.
questions.explanation: um … zu works only when the same person acts and has the goal, and it has no subject of its own: "um ein Auto zu kaufen", "um in Ruhe zu lernen", "um pünktlich anzukommen" (zu inside the separable verb). When the subjects differ, German needs damit + verb at the end: "damit ich studieren kann", "damit wir ihn verstehen".

questions.stem: Name the numbered places on this campus.

image.alt: A campus map with five numbered places: a hall with curved rows of seats and a lectern, a building full of bookshelves, a building with a plate, knife and fork, a block with many windows and a bed, and a round yellow sign with a green H.

questions.explanation: 1 rows of seats facing a lectern: der Hörsaal (lecture hall). 2 bookshelves: die Bibliothek. 3 plate and cutlery: die Mensa (university canteen). 4 many small rooms with beds: das Studentenwohnheim (hall of residence). 5 the green H on a yellow sign marks a bus stop in Germany: die Bushaltestelle. A Seminar is a small class, not a building, and a Fachhochschule is a whole institution.

questions.stem: Match each beginning to the ending that completes it correctly.
left: Statt für die Klausur zu lernen,
choices: damit die Studierenden ihr Deutsch verbessern.
questions.explanation: ohne … zu + infinitive = without -ing; a fronted statt … zu clause is followed by the main verb ("hat er"); damit introduces a goal for a different subject (the university offers, the students improve); brauchen nicht … zu = don't have to. "um du es verstehst" mixes um with a subject, and "ohne lesen" copies the English -ing pattern.

questions.stem: Complete with da, falls or sodass, using each word once: "___ Sie umgezogen sind, müssen Sie Ihre Adresse ändern." / "Rufen Sie uns an, ___ Sie Fragen haben." / "Ich habe die Frist verpasst, ___ der Vertrag automatisch verlängert wurde."
questions.explanation: 1: a known reason at the start of the sentence: Da (weil is also grammatical). 2: a possibility you prepare for: falls (wenn also works). 3: a result of missing the deadline: sodass (also spelled so dass). All three send the verb to the end.

questions.stem: This timeline shows a 12-month contract. Name each numbered part.

image.alt: A timeline of a mobile phone contract in 2026 with five numbered parts: the line at 1 January, the long bar from January to December, a short block in December after 30 November, the line at 31 December, and a dashed arrow into 2027.

questions.explanation: 1 the contract starts on 1 January (der Vertragsbeginn). 2 it runs for twelve months (die Laufzeit). 3 the last month is the notice period (die Kündigungsfrist): you must cancel before it begins, by 30 November. 4 it ends on 31 December (das Vertragsende). 5 if nobody cancels, it is renewed (die Verlängerung). Selbstbeteiligung (excess) and Schadensfall (claim) belong to insurance claims, not to the timeline.

questions.stem: Put the steps of an insurance claim in order, as in Tobias's letter.
questions.explanation: First the damage happens (the bike is stolen), then Tobias reports it. The insurer can't process the claim until the missing documents arrive, and it pays compensation (current value minus the excess) only after processing the case.

questions.stem: Which words are linking adverbs, followed straight away by the verb when they start a sentence (like deshalb)? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: daher, deswegen and also (so, therefore) are linking adverbs: Daher können wir nicht zahlen. sodass, falls and da (since) are subordinating conjunctions: they send the verb to the end of their own clause (da es regnet, falls Sie Fragen haben).

questions.stem: Match each connector to its meaning.
questions.explanation: da gives a reason the reader already knows; falls a possibility; sodass a result; daher is the formal "therefore"; also means "so, therefore" (a false friend: English "also" is auch). "in order that" is a goal, which is damit (lesson 7).

questions.stem: Complete the pairs: "Ich habe ___ Zeit noch Geld." / "Wir fahren ___ heute oder morgen." / "Sie spricht nicht nur Deutsch, ___ auch Polnisch."
questions.explanation: weder … noch (neither … nor), entweder … oder (either … or), nicht nur … sondern auch (not only … but also). After nicht nur the partner is sondern, never aber.

questions.stem: Name the four kinds of building.

image.alt: Four numbered buildings in a row: a detached house with a fence and a tree, three joined narrow houses, a four-storey block of flats, and a tall tower with many floors.

questions.explanation: 1 a house for one family standing on its own: das Einfamilienhaus. 2 houses joined in a row: das Reihenhaus. 3 a building with flats for several families: das Mehrfamilienhaus. 4 a tall tower block: das Hochhaus. A WG is a flat-share (a way of living, not a building), and das Treppenhaus is the stairwell inside a building.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Ich habe weder kein Auto noch kein Fahrrad.
Sowohl Tom als auch Lea wohnen in einer WG.
Die Wohnung ist nicht nur laut, aber auch teuer.
Die Wohnung ist nicht nur laut, sondern auch teuer.
Entweder du sprichst mit den Nachbarn, oder ich mache es.
questions.explanation: sowohl … als auch adds the subjects, so the verb is plural (wohnen). nicht nur is followed by sondern auch, not aber auch. entweder can stand in position 0, so "Entweder du sprichst …" is fine. weder … noch is already negative: "weder ein Auto noch ein Fahrrad", without kein.

questions.stem: A flat may have a balcony (B) and a garden (G). Match each sentence pattern to what it says.
left: nicht nur B, sondern auch G
choices: both, with the second as extra news
questions.explanation: sowohl … als auch = both; weder … noch = neither; entweder … oder = one or the other; nicht nur … sondern auch also means both, but presents the second item as the surprising addition.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "Neither the landlord nor the caretaker has got in touch." The capitalised word comes first.
questions.explanation: Weder der Vermieter noch die Hausmeisterin hat sich gemeldet. The whole subject "weder der Vermieter noch die Hausmeisterin" fills position 1, the verb "hat" comes second, the reflexive pronoun follows, and the participle "gemeldet" goes to the end. (With weder … noch, "haben" in the plural would also be correct.)

questions.stem: Complete with the comparative: "Je ___ (früh) du anfängst, desto ___ (leicht) ist es."
questions.explanation: je and desto are each followed by a comparative: früh → früher, leicht → leichter. The je part has the verb at the end (anfängst); the desto part has the verb straight after the comparative (ist es).

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "The more I train, the fitter I get." The capitalised words come first.
questions.explanation: Je mehr ich trainiere, desto fitter werde ich. In the je clause the verb goes to the end; in the desto clause "desto fitter" fills position 1, so the verb "werde" comes next and the subject "ich" after it.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Lisa ist die am schnellsten Läuferin.
Immer mehr Menschen gehen ins Fitnessstudio.
questions.explanation: Before a noun the superlative takes der/die/das + -ste + ending (die schnellste Läuferin); without a noun it is am + -sten (läuft am schnellsten). am never stands before a noun. A comparative before a noun needs its ending too: einen besseren Trainer. immer + comparative (immer mehr) means "more and more".

questions.stem: Look at the race result. Match each runner to the sentence about her.

image.alt: A podium for a 10 km city run: Lea first in 41:20, Aylin second in 43:05, Mia third in 44:50.

choices: war schneller als Mia, aber langsamer als Lea.
questions.explanation: Lea had the shortest time (41:20), so she ran the fastest. Aylin (43:05) was between the two. Mia's 44:50 is the longest time. Nobody was faster than Lea.

questions.stem: Match each adjective to its superlative before a noun.
questions.explanation: gut → beste, hoch → höchste (with ch again), nah → nächste (with ch), viel → meiste, groß → größte (no extra e). "höhste" and "größeste" are typical mistakes.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ich trinke gern Kaffee, ___ mein Mann nur Tee trinkt."
questions.explanation: Two different tastes side by side, and neither should prevent the other: a contrast, so während (whereas). obwohl would say that his tea-drinking should stop me drinking coffee. trotzdem and deshalb are adverbs and would need the verb straight after them.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Er zahlt bar, wohingegen ich zahle mit Karte.
Er zahlt bar, wohingegen zahle ich mit Karte.
Er zahlt bar, wohingegen mit Karte ich zahle.
Er zahlt bar, wohingegen ich mit Karte zahle.
questions.explanation: wohingegen is a subordinating conjunction like während, so the conjugated verb "zahle" goes to the end: wohingegen ich mit Karte zahle. The other versions use main-clause or random word order.

questions.stem: Complete: "Die Miete in München ist sehr hoch. In Leipzig hingegen ___ niedriger."
questions.explanation: "In Leipzig hingegen" counts as one block in position 1, so the verb comes next and then the subject: "In Leipzig hingegen ist sie viel niedriger." hingegen is a linking adverb, not a conjunction, so the verb does not go to the end.

questions.stem: What does dagegen mean in these two sentences? (a) "Ich bin dagegen." (b) "In Wien dagegen ist es ruhiger."
choices: (a) against it, (b) on the other hand
(a) on the other hand, (b) against it
questions.explanation: In (a) dagegen is the da-word of gegen: "I'm against it." In (b) it compares Vienna with another place: "In Vienna, on the other hand, it's quieter." The context (a comparison or not) tells you which one is meant.

questions.stem: "War die Reise teuer?" – "Allerdings!" What does the answer mean?
questions.explanation: As a short answer on its own, Allerdings! is strong agreement: "It certainly was!" Inside a sentence allerdings means "however, though" and limits what was said before.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "We'll have a barbecue tomorrow unless it rains"?
choices: Wir grillen morgen, es sei denn, es regnet.
Wir grillen morgen, es sei denn, es regnet nicht.
Wir grillen morgen, es sei denn, es morgen regnet.
Wir grillen morgen, außer wenn es regnet nicht.
questions.explanation: es sei denn is followed by a normal main clause with the verb in second place ("es regnet"), and it already contains the "not" of unless. Adding nicht turns it into "unless it doesn't rain". Putting the verb at the end after es sei denn is wrong unless you add dass ("es sei denn, dass es regnet"). außer wenn would also work, but without the nicht: "außer wenn es regnet".

questions.stem: Look at the sign. It is an ordinary Sunday, 10:30. Lukas wants to buy two rolls for 1.20 euros. What is true?

image.alt: A bakery door sign: Bäckerei Krume. Öffnungszeiten: Mo – Fr 6:30 – 18:30, Sa 7:00 – 13:00, So 8:00 – 11:00. Feiertags geschlossen. Kartenzahlung ab 10 €.

choices: The bakery is closed, so he can't buy anything.
He can pay by card because it is Sunday.
He can buy them, but he has to pay cash.
He can only buy them after 11:00.
questions.explanation: On Sundays (So) the bakery is open from 8:00 to 11:00, so at 10:30 it is open. Card payment is only possible from 10 euros (Kartenzahlung ab 10 €), so for 1.20 euros he has to pay cash. It closes at 11:00, it doesn't open then.

questions.stem: Rewrite the bakery rule with es sei denn: "Man kann nur bar bezahlen, es sei denn, man ___ mindestens 10 Euro ___." (ausgeben)
questions.explanation: After es sei denn comes a normal main clause: the conjugated verb in second place (gibt) and the separable prefix at the end (aus): "es sei denn, man gibt mindestens 10 Euro aus". With außer wenn the verb would go to the end and join up: "außer wenn man mindestens 10 Euro ausgibt".

questions.stem: Complete: "In Hamburg regnet es oft, ___ es in München mehr Sonne gibt." (whereas) / "Das Hotel war schön. ___ war das Frühstück teuer." (however)
questions.explanation: 1: a contrast with the verb (gibt) at the end: während or wohingegen (or the less common wogegen). 2: the verb (war) comes straight after the gap, so it must be a linking adverb in position 1: Allerdings (or Jedoch). aber is position 0 and would need "Aber das Frühstück war teuer".

questions.stem: Match each connector to the word order that follows it.
choices: comma and a normal main clause
questions.explanation: während, wohingegen and außer wenn are subordinating: verb at the end. hingegen, dagegen and allerdings are linking adverbs: verb straight after them in position 1. es sei denn is followed by a comma and a main clause with the verb second (es sei denn, es regnet). Only und, aber, oder, denn and sondern leave the order unchanged.

questions.stem: Which sentences express a contrast (two different things side by side) rather than a concession? Select all that apply.
choices: Meine Schwester ist ordentlich, während ich lieber im Chaos lebe.
Obwohl es regnet, gehen wir spazieren.
Ich trinke Kaffee. Mein Mann hingegen trinkt Tee.
Im Gegensatz zu dir koche ich nicht gern.
Das Auto ist alt. Trotzdem fährt es gut.
questions.explanation: während, hingegen and im Gegensatz zu put two different people side by side; you could swap the halves without changing the meaning. obwohl and trotzdem are concessive: rain should stop a walk, and age should stop a car running well.

questions.stem: Put the words in order: "Unlike my brother, I don't speak French." The capitalised words come first.
questions.explanation: Im Gegensatz zu meinem Bruder spreche ich kein Französisch. The phrase "im Gegensatz zu meinem Bruder" (zu + dative) fills position 1, so the verb "spreche" comes next and the subject "ich" follows it.

questions.stem: In Jake's blog post, what does he say about punctuality?
choices: Germans are always on time, and trains too.
His flatmate thinks arriving early looks uninterested.
Germans are sometimes late too, but for appointments it is better to come a little early.
questions.explanation: "Im Gegensatz zu meinen Erwartungen kommen auch Deutsche manchmal zu spät": contrary to his expectations, Germans are sometimes late too. His flatmate's advice is to come five minutes early to appointments, "andernfalls denken die Leute, du hast kein Interesse": otherwise people think you aren't interested.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: das Vorurteil = prejudice (literally a judgement made beforehand); die Gemeinsamkeit = something in common; vergleichbar = comparable; der Ladenschluss = closing time of shops; andernfalls = otherwise (formal sonst). A difference is der Unterschied, and punctuality is die Pünktlichkeit.

questions.stem: Complete: "___ es morgen schneien sollte, fahren wir los."
questions.explanation: Tomorrow's snow is only a possibility (sollte), and it won't change the plan: auch wenn (even if). obwohl is only for real facts, weil gives a reason (snow is no reason to leave), and trotzdem is an adverb that can't introduce a clause.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Selbst wenn ich habe Zeit, gehe ich nicht.
Selbst wenn ich Zeit habe, ich gehe nicht.
Selbst wenn ich Zeit habe, gehe ich nicht.
Selbst ich Zeit habe, gehe ich nicht.
questions.explanation: selbst wenn sends the verb to the end (ich Zeit habe), and when the clause comes first, the main verb follows straight after the comma (gehe ich). selbst alone, without wenn, can't introduce a clause.

questions.stem: Which sentence describes an extreme, imagined case?
choices: Selbst wenn ich im Lotto gewinnen würde, würde ich weiterarbeiten.
Obwohl ich müde bin, arbeite ich weiter.
Weil ich müde bin, gehe ich ins Bett.
Wenn ich müde bin, trinke ich Kaffee.
questions.explanation: selbst wenn with würde imagines an extreme case (winning the lottery) that would still not change the result. The obwohl sentence states a real fact, the weil sentence a reason, and the wenn sentence an ordinary condition.

questions.stem: Why is "Obwohl es morgen schneit, fahren wir los" wrong?
choices: obwohl needs the verb in second position.
obwohl is only for real facts, and tomorrow's weather is not a fact yet.
An obwohl clause must be followed by trotzdem.
questions.explanation: obwohl concedes a fact that is true. Tomorrow's snow is only possible, so German uses auch wenn (or selbst wenn): "Auch wenn es morgen schneit, fahren wir los." The word order of the sentence is fine, and obwohl clauses can come first.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Egal, wie teuer ist es, ich kaufe es.
Egal, wie es teuer ist, kaufe ich es.
Egal wie teuer, es ist ich kaufe.
Egal, wie teuer es ist, ich kaufe es.
questions.explanation: The wie clause has the verb at the end, with wie and its adjective together (wie teuer es ist). The egal clause stands outside the main sentence, so the main clause keeps its normal order, subject first: "ich kaufe es".

questions.stem: In an essay you have given one argument for card payment and want to add a second one for the same side. Which beginning fits?
questions.explanation: Darüber hinaus (moreover) adds another argument to the same side. Auf der anderen Seite and Dagegen spricht switch to the other side, and Zusammenfassend lässt sich sagen starts the conclusion.

questions.stem: Write the missing first word of each signpost: "___ kommt, dass Geschäfte weniger Arbeit haben." (added to this) / "___ lässt sich sagen: Karte ja, aber Bargeld auch." (to sum up)
questions.explanation: Hinzu kommt, dass … (added to this, …) adds an argument in a dass clause. Zusammenfassend lässt sich sagen … (to sum up, …) introduces the conclusion.

questions.stem: Write the verb in the right form: "Darüber hinaus ___ man kein Geld abheben." (müssen) / "Auch wenn es teuer ___, kaufe ich es." (sein)
questions.explanation: darüber hinaus is a linking adverb: the conjugated verb comes straight after it, then the subject: "Darüber hinaus muss man …". auch wenn sends the verb to the end of its clause: "Auch wenn es teuer ist, …".

questions.stem: Put the paragraphs of the model essay "Sollte man das Bargeld abschaffen?" in the order they appear.
choices: The question, with the Bundesbank study
Weighing up and the writer's own view
questions.explanation: The essay follows the standard shape: an introduction that presents the question, the arguments for card payment (zunächst, darüber hinaus, hinzu kommt), the counterarguments (auf der anderen Seite), and finally the weighing up and conclusion (wie man es auch dreht, letztlich, zusammenfassend).

questions.stem: Which arguments in the model essay speak for keeping cash? Select all that apply.
choices: Cash works when the power fails.
Not everyone copes well with cards and apps.
A stolen card can be blocked at once.
questions.explanation: The paragraph that starts "Auf der anderen Seite" gives the arguments for cash: anonymity (no data), it works without internet or power, and not everyone copes with cards and apps. Speed, contactless payment and blocking a stolen card are arguments for card payment.

questions.stem: Match each signpost to its job in an essay.
choices: concedes a point and answers it
gives the reason for a single fact
questions.explanation: Zunächst opens the first argument, darüber hinaus adds one, auf der anderen Seite turns to the opposite side, es stimmt zwar … aber concedes and answers, and zusammenfassend starts the conclusion. A reason for a single fact is weil or da, not an essay signpost.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: die Münze = coin; der Geldschein = banknote; kontaktlos = contactless; abwägen = to weigh up (separable: ich wäge ab); das Gegenargument = counterargument. To withdraw money is Geld abheben, and a credit card is die Kreditkarte.

questions.stem: According to the model essay, what did the 2023 Bundesbank study find?
choices: Cash is hardly used in Germany any more.
Cash is still the most-used means of payment at the checkout, but its share is falling.
Most Germans pay only with their phones.
Card payments are becoming less common.
questions.explanation: "Bargeld ist in Deutschland an der Kasse zwar noch das meistgenutzte Zahlungsmittel, sein Anteil sinkt aber": cash is still the most-used means of payment at the checkout, but its share is falling. Note the zwar … aber that concedes one point and adds another.

questions.stem: What is the writer's conclusion in the model essay?
choices: Cash should be abolished because cards are more practical.
The writer only ever pays cash.
Cards are fine, but cash should continue to exist.
Neither side has any good arguments.
questions.explanation: "Zusammenfassend lässt sich sagen: Karte ja, aber Bargeld sollte es weiter geben." The writer usually pays by card but is against abolishing cash, "auch wenn sie praktisch wäre", because people should be free to choose how they pay. Both sides, the writer says, have good arguments.

questions.stem: Complete with relative pronouns: "Das sind die Kollegen, mit ___ ich mich gut verstehe. Meine Schwester, ___ ich alles erzähle, wohnt in Wien."
questions.explanation: "mit" takes the dative, and "die Kollegen" is plural, so the dative plural "denen" (never "den"). "jemandem etwas erzählen": the person you tell is in the dative, and "meine Schwester" is feminine, so the dative feminine "der".

questions.stem: Put the parts in order to say "That's the colleague I often argue with." Start with "Das ist der Kollege,".
questions.explanation: The preposition and the relative pronoun stay together at the front of the relative clause ("mit dem"), never at the end as in English. Then the subject and the reflexive pronoun, the adverb, and the conjugated verb last: "Das ist der Kollege, mit dem ich mich oft streite."

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Das sind die Leute, denen das Haus gehört.
Ich kenne eine Frau, deren Mann Arzt ist.
Die Kinder, den ich helfe, sind sehr nett.
Das ist die Kollegin, die ich mit arbeite.
Das Problem, über das wir diskutiert haben, ist gelöst.
questions.explanation: "gehören" takes the dative, so "denen" (dative plural) is right; "deren" agrees with the owner "eine Frau" (feminine); "über das" puts the preposition first, with the accusative. "Die Kinder, den ich helfe" needs the dative plural "denen", and "die ich mit arbeite" leaves the preposition at the end, English-style: it must be "mit der ich arbeite".

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this sentence: "Das ist die Kollegin, mit der ich ein Büro teile."

image.alt: The sentence "Das ist die Kollegin, mit der ich ein Büro teile." in boxes. Four boxes are numbered: "die Kollegin", "mit", "der" and "teile."

questions.explanation: 1 "die Kollegin" is the antecedent: it gives the gender and number (feminine singular). 2 "mit" is the preposition: it decides the case (dative). 3 "der" is the relative pronoun, dative feminine. 4 "teile" is the conjugated verb, at the end of the relative clause. The subject of the main clause is "das", which isn't numbered.

questions.stem: Match each beginning to the relative pronoun that fills the gap.
left: die Freunde, ___ ich am meisten vertraue
der Bruder, mit ___ ich mich oft streite
die Kritik, über ___ ich mich geärgert habe
die Nachbarin, ___ Hund jede Nacht bellt
das Kind, ___ Eltern noch nicht da sind
questions.explanation: "vertrauen" takes the dative: plural "denen". "mit" + dative masculine: "dem". "sich ärgern über" + accusative, feminine: "die". "whose" agrees with the owner: "die Nachbarin" (feminine) → "deren"; "das Kind" (neuter) → "dessen".

questions.stem: Complete with one word each: "Das ist alles, ___ ich über die Stadt weiß." and "Das ist das Café, ___ wir uns kennengelernt haben."
questions.explanation: After "alles" the relative pronoun is "was", not "das". For a place, "wo" can replace "in dem": "das Café, wo wir uns kennengelernt haben" (= "in dem wir uns kennengelernt haben", which is two words).

questions.stem: Name the numbered sights in this old town.

image.alt: An old town with a large church with two towers, a town hall with a clock, a castle on a hill, a statue on a pedestal, a fountain and an open-air stage. Six things are numbered.

questions.explanation: 1 is the cathedral with two towers (der Dom), 2 the castle on the hill (die Burg: built for defence; das Schloss is a palace), 3 the town hall with its clock (das Rathaus), 4 the fountain (der Brunnen), 5 the statue on its pedestal (das Denkmal) and 6 the open-air stage (die Bühne).

questions.stem: Match each beginning to the relative word that fills the gap.
left: Das ist alles, ___ wir gesprochen haben.
die Stadt, ___ wir im Sommer fahren
questions.explanation: "sprechen über" after "alles" needs a wo(r)- word: "worüber". Movement towards a place: "wohin"; origin: "woher". After "etwas" (like alles, nichts) German uses "was". After a real noun with a gender (das Buch) the relative pronoun is "das". "wo" is for a place with no movement.

questions.stem: In which sentences is "was" the right word for the gap? Select all that apply.
choices: Es gibt nichts, ___ mich hier stört.
Das ist das Schönste, ___ ich je gesehen habe.
Der Zug kam zu spät, ___ mich sehr geärgert hat.
Das ist das Gemälde, ___ mir am besten gefällt.
Die Stadt, ___ ich wohne, ist klein.
questions.explanation: "was" follows "nichts", a superlative used as a noun (das Schönste) and a whole clause (the train being late annoyed me). "das Gemälde" is a real noun, so "das"; for a place where someone lives, "wo" or "in der".

questions.stem: Put the words in order to say "That's everything we talked about." Start with "Das".
questions.explanation: Main clause first ("Das ist alles"), then the relative clause starting with "worüber" (über + was becomes worüber), and the verb at the end: "gesprochen haben".

questions.stem: Put the words in brackets into the genitive: "das Haus ___" (der Vater), "die Fotos ___" (die Kinder), "der Name ___" (der Kollege).
questions.explanation: Masculine: "des" and -s on the noun: des Vaters. Plural: "der" and no ending: der Kinder. "Kollege" is an n-noun, so it takes -n and no -s: des Kollegen.

questions.stem: This is Jonas's family tree. Jonas is "ich". Choose the genitive phrase that describes each numbered person from his point of view.

image.alt: A family tree with names only. Top row: Karl and Ilse. Middle row: Michael married to Sabine, and Sabine's brother Peter; Karl and Ilse are the parents of Sabine and Peter. Bottom row: Jonas (ich), the son of Michael and Sabine, and Lea, Peter's daughter. Karl, Ilse, Peter and Lea are numbered.

questions.explanation: Jonas's mother is Sabine. Her parents Karl and Ilse are "der Vater meiner Mutter" and "die Mutter meiner Mutter" (feminine genitive: meiner, no ending on Mutter). Peter is her brother, "der Bruder meiner Mutter", so he is Jonas's uncle, and Lea is "die Tochter meines Onkels" (masculine genitive: meines Onkels).

questions.stem: Match each noun to its genitive singular form.
questions.explanation: "Name" is one of the few n-nouns with -ns: des Namens. Nouns ending in -s take -es (des Hauses), and -nis doubles the s (des Zeugnisses). "Herr" is an n-noun: des Herrn. Feminine nouns never add an ending: der Mutter.

questions.stem: Which phrases are correct written German? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Names take -s with no apostrophe (Annas), and only an apostrophe after an s sound (Klaus'). "Anna's" with an apostrophe is English influence. "Kollege" is an n-noun: des Kollegen, with no -s. "am Ende des langen Tages" is right: -en on the adjective after an article, -es on the noun.

questions.stem: Put the words in order to say "Anna's grandfather built the house." Start with "Annas".
questions.explanation: A name in the genitive comes before its noun: "Annas Großvater" is the subject in position 1, the auxiliary "hat" is in position 2, and the participle "gebaut" goes to the end.

questions.stem: Complete with genitive prepositions: "___ des Streiks fahren heute keine Züge." (because of) and "___ der Verspätung haben wir den Anschluss noch bekommen." (despite)
questions.explanation: "wegen" means because of, "trotz" means despite; both take the genitive in written German: wegen des Streiks, trotz der Verspätung. (The more formal "aufgrund", from the honors lesson, is also right in the first gap.)

questions.stem: Match each preposition to its meaning.
questions.explanation: These are the six genitive prepositions of the lesson. "according to" would be "laut" and "thanks to" would be "dank", which are not among them.

questions.stem: Which phrases are correct in written standard German? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "wegen des starken Regens" and "während der ganzen Fahrt" are genitives with -en on the adjective. A number without an article can't show the genitive, so "innerhalb von zwei Wochen" needs "von". "trotz den Streik" is accusative, which is wrong both in writing (trotz des Streiks) and in speech (trotz dem Streik). "innerhalb einem Monat" uses the spoken dative where the genitive can be shown: write "innerhalb eines Monats".

questions.stem: Look at the departure board. Which sentence is true?

image.alt: A departure board at Frankfurt (Main) Hauptbahnhof. 14:12, ICE 578 to Hamburg, platform 7: about 40 minutes later, fault at the signal box. 14:20, RE 4512 to Fulda, platform 5: cancelled because of staff shortage. 14:30, RE 4518 to Hanau: today from platform 3 instead of platform 4. 14:45, RB 15 to Gelnhausen: replacement buses because of construction work.

choices: Der ICE nach Hamburg fällt wegen eines Streiks aus.
Der RE nach Hanau hat 40 Minuten Verspätung.
Wegen Personalmangels fällt der Zug nach Fulda aus.
Trotz der Bauarbeiten fährt die RB nach Gelnhausen normal.
questions.explanation: The 14:20 to Fulda "fällt aus wegen Personalmangels": it is cancelled because of a staff shortage. The ICE to Hamburg is about 40 minutes late because of a fault, not cancelled; the RE to Hanau only leaves from a different platform; and because of the construction work there are replacement buses to Gelnhausen instead of the train.

questions.stem: Put the parts in order to say "The flight was cancelled because of the storm." Start with "Wegen".
questions.explanation: The prepositional phrase "Wegen des Unwetters" fills position 1, so the auxiliary "ist" comes next in position 2, then the subject "der Flug", and the participle "ausgefallen" at the end (ausfallen takes sein).

questions.stem: Choose the right phrase for each numbered picture.

image.alt: Four pictures, numbered: a burning candle, a child asleep in bed, pieces of broken glass on the floor, and a tree lying on the ground next to its stump.

questions.explanation: The candle is burning and the child is sleeping now: present participles, brennend and schlafend. The glass is already broken and the tree has already fallen over: past participles, zerbrochen and umgefallen. "das geschlafene Kind" is impossible (schlafen has no object and takes haben), and "die gebrannte Kerze" is wrong because the candle is still burning, which needs the present participle.

questions.stem: Write the adjective in brackets with the right ending: "wegen ___ Wetters" (schlecht), "mit ___ Obst" (frisch), "viele ___ Kunden" (zufrieden).
questions.explanation: With no article the adjective shows the case itself, except in the masculine and neuter genitive, where the noun already has -s: wegen schlechten Wetters. Dative neuter: frischem (like "dem"). After "viele" the ending is strong: viele zufriedene Kunden (like "die").

questions.stem: Match each phrase to its meaning.
choices: the bike that has been repaired
the bike that is repairing something
questions.explanation: A present participle (steigend, weinend) means the noun is doing it now. A past participle of a verb with an object (repariert, bestellt) is passive: something was done to the noun. "steigen" takes sein, so "gestiegen" is active and finished: the prices have risen.

questions.stem: In which phrases does the adjective take a strong ending (the ending of the definite article)? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: After "viele", with no article (mit kaltem Wasser, like "dem") and in the feminine genitive with no article (guter, like "der"), the adjective shows the case: strong endings. After "alle" and "der" the article shows the case, so the ending is weak (-e or -en).

questions.stem: Put the words in order to say "Please hand in the completed forms." Start with "Bitte".
questions.explanation: A polite instruction: the verb "geben" first after "Bitte", then "Sie", the object, and the separable prefix "ab" at the end. The participle "ausgefüllten" stands between the article and the noun like any adjective.

questions.stem: Which noun does the article "Die" belong to? "Die im Sommer bei Bauarbeiten am Marktplatz entdeckten Münzen stammen aus der Römerzeit."
questions.explanation: "Sommer", "Bauarbeiten" and "Marktplatz" each come with their own preposition (im, bei, am), so they belong inside the phrase. The noun that "Die" belongs to is "Münzen", right after the participle "entdeckten": the coins that were discovered.

questions.stem: What does "die seit Februar laufenden Bauarbeiten" mean?
choices: the construction work that has been going on since February
the construction work that ended in February
the construction work that will start in February
the runners at the construction site since February
questions.explanation: "laufend" is the present participle of "laufen": the work is still going on, and "seit Februar" belongs to it. As a relative clause: die Bauarbeiten, die seit Februar laufen. "laufen" here means "to be in progress", not running.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this phrase: "der beim Bau der neuen Brücke entdeckte Schatz".

image.alt: The phrase "der beim Bau der neuen Brücke entdeckte Schatz" in four numbered boxes, with a bracket joining "der" and "Schatz".

questions.explanation: The article "der" and the noun "Schatz" frame the phrase. "beim Bau der neuen Brücke" is the participle's own expansion (when it was discovered), and "entdeckte" is the participle with the adjective ending -e, right before the noun. There is no relative pronoun and no conjugated verb: that's what makes it a phrase, not a clause.

questions.stem: Turn the relative clause into a participle phrase: "der Zug, der gerade angekommen ist" → "der gerade ___ Zug". Write one word.
questions.explanation: "ankommen" takes sein, so its participle is active: the train that has arrived. Before the noun it takes the weak ending after "der": der gerade angekommene Zug.

questions.stem: Turn the relative clause into a participle phrase: "die Münzen, die von Kindern gefunden wurden" → "die von Kindern ___ Münzen". Write one word.
questions.explanation: Delete "die … wurden", move "von Kindern gefunden" before the noun and give the participle its ending: after "die" in the plural the ending is -en: die von Kindern gefundenen Münzen.

questions.stem: Put the parts in order to say "the strike that had been announced for weeks". Start with "der".
questions.explanation: The article and the noun frame the phrase; the participle "angekündigte" stands directly before the noun, and its expansion "seit Wochen" comes before the participle: der seit Wochen angekündigte Streik.

questions.stem: Match each phrase to the relative clause with the same meaning.
choices: die Brücke, die geplant werden muss
questions.explanation: Partizip I is active and happening now (die Preise, die steigen). "steigen" takes sein, so "gestiegen" is active and finished (die gestiegen sind). "planen" has an object, so "geplant" is passive (die geplant wurde). zu + Partizip I means "must be done" (die geplant werden muss).

questions.stem: Which phrases are correct German? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "angekommen" (a sein verb), "liegend" (Partizip I) and the adjective "geeignet" all work before a noun. "schlafen" takes haben and has no object, so it has no Partizip II before a noun: say "der Mann, der lange geschlafen hat". In "der entdeckte beim Bau Schatz" the expansion comes after the participle, English-style; it must come before: der beim Bau entdeckte Schatz.

questions.stem: What does "die noch zu prüfenden Anträge" mean?
choices: the applications that are still checking something
the applications that still have to be checked
the applications that have already been checked
the applications in order to check
questions.explanation: zu + Partizip I before a noun (the gerundive) is passive and means that something must be done: die Anträge, die noch geprüft werden müssen. It is not an infinitive with zu, and it doesn't say the checking has happened.

questions.stem: Which relative clause means the same as "die von der Stadt finanzierte Ausgrabung"?
choices: die Ausgrabung, die die Stadt finanzieren muss
die Stadt, die die Ausgrabung finanziert
die Ausgrabung, die von der Stadt finanziert wird
die Ausgrabung, mit der sich die Stadt finanziert
questions.explanation: "finanzieren" has an object, so the Partizip II is passive, and "von der Stadt" is the agent: die Ausgrabung, die von der Stadt finanziert wird (or wurde). "finanzieren muss" would be the meaning of zu + Partizip I, and the phrase is about the excavation, not the town.

questions.stem: According to the news report "Römischer Schatz unter dem Marktplatz", what did the workers come across?
choices: a Roman helmet made of several parts
a clay pot covered with stones, with silver coins inside
an old wall lying in the ground
questions.explanation: "stießen Arbeiter auf ein mit Steinen abgedecktes Tongefäß. Darin lagen 312 Silbermünzen." The 40 coins were the previous record in Kronstein; the helmet and the wall come from the lesson's examples.

questions.stem: The report says: "Die bereits ausgegrabenen, aber noch zu untersuchenden Münzen sollen im Herbst im Stadtmuseum ausgestellt werden." What does this tell you?
choices: The coins are still in the ground; they will be dug up in the autumn.
The coins have been examined and are already in the museum.
The coins have been dug up but still have to be examined; they are to be shown in the autumn.
The museum wants to sell the coins in the autumn.
questions.explanation: "bereits ausgegrabenen" = already dug up (passive, finished); "noch zu untersuchenden" = still to be examined (zu + Partizip I: must be done); "sollen … ausgestellt werden" = are to be exhibited.

questions.stem: Complete with one verb: "Die Münzen ___ aus dem 2. Jahrhundert." (date from)
questions.explanation: "stammen aus" means to come from or to date from: Die Münzen stammen aus dem 2. Jahrhundert. The subject is plural, so the verb is "stammen".

questions.stem: Complete: "Wir besuchten die im 12. Jahrhundert gebaut___ Burg."
questions.explanation: The frame is "die … Burg", feminine accusative after "besuchten". After "die" the adjective (here the participle) takes the weak ending -e: die im 12. Jahrhundert gebaute Burg.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence from an official letter: "___ der Bauarbeiten bleibt die Straße bis Mai gesperrt."
questions.explanation: The construction work is the reason, so "aufgrund" (because of, the formal "wegen"). "dank" is only for a good result, "anlässlich" means on the occasion of, and "mithilfe" means with the help of.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses "dank" in a way that sounds ironic or wrong?
choices: Dank deiner Hilfe habe ich die Prüfung bestanden.
Dank der neuen Heizung ist die Wohnung warm.
Dank des Streiks kamen wir zwei Stunden zu spät.
Dank vieler Spenden konnte der Spielplatz gebaut werden.
questions.explanation: "dank" means thanks to and is only used for a cause with a good result. Arriving two hours late because of a strike is not good, so here you need "wegen" or "aufgrund": Wegen des Streiks kamen wir zwei Stunden zu spät.

questions.stem: Match each preposition to its meaning.
questions.explanation: aufgrund = due to, because of; infolge = as a result of; angesichts = in view of; bezüglich = regarding; anlässlich = on the occasion of; mithilfe = with the help of. "instead of" is statt and "despite" is trotz (lesson 14).

questions.stem: Complete with "dessen" or "deren": "Anwohner, ___ Garage in der gesperrten Zone liegt, erhalten einen Parkausweis." and "Herr Kaya, ___ Antrag noch nicht vollständig ist, bekommt einen Brief."
questions.explanation: "dessen" and "deren" agree with the owner. "Anwohner" is plural, so "deren Garage" (even though Garage is feminine singular, that doesn't matter). "Herr Kaya" is masculine, so "dessen Antrag".

questions.stem: Complete: "Das ist die Mieterin, mit ___ kleinem Sohn ich manchmal Fußball spiele."
questions.explanation: The owner "die Mieterin" is feminine, so "deren". "mit" goes in front and makes "kleinem Sohn" dative; the adjective takes the strong ending -em because there is no article after deren. "dessen" is for a masculine or neuter owner, and "ihrem" would make a main clause, so the verb couldn't be at the end.

questions.stem: Which phrases are correct standard written German? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "laut" with a noun without an article takes no ending (laut Fahrplan); "entlang" after the noun takes the accusative (den Fluss entlang); "aufgrund von" is used before a noun without an article. "dem Vater sein Haus" is the spoken possessive dative: write "das Haus des Vaters". After "mangels" the feminine genitive with no article is "ausreichender Nachfrage".

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this official letter.

image.alt: An official letter from Stadt Kronstein, Tiefbauamt, to Frau Petra Berger about the renovation of Lindenstraße. Six parts are numbered: the line at the top, the address block, the date on the right, the bold subject line, the greeting and the closing.

questions.explanation: 1 is the sender (der Absender: the town office), 2 the recipient's address (der Empfänger), 3 the place and date (das Datum), 4 the bold subject line (der Betreff), 5 the greeting (die Anrede: Sehr geehrte Frau Berger,) and 6 the closing (die Grußformel: Mit freundlichen Grüßen).

questions.stem: According to the letter from the Tiefbauamt, who can get a free parking permit?
choices: residents whose garage is in the closed zone, if they apply
only Frau Berger, because she asked
questions.explanation: "Anwohner, deren Garage in der gesperrten Zone liegt, erhalten auf Antrag einen kostenlosen Parkausweis": residents whose garage is in the closed zone receive one on application (auf Antrag), not automatically.

questions.stem: According to the letter, why will the work take two weeks less than first planned?
choices: thanks to the support of the municipal utilities
because of a burst pipe in January
because Frau Berger made an enquiry
in view of the long construction period
questions.explanation: "Dank der Unterstützung der Stadtwerke dauern die Arbeiten zwei Wochen kürzer als ursprünglich geplant." The burst pipe is why the pipes must be replaced, and "angesichts der langen Bauzeit" introduces the request for understanding.

questions.stem: Put the parts in order to say "Lindenstraße is closed because of the renovation." Start with "Aufgrund".
questions.explanation: "Aufgrund der Sanierung" fills position 1, the verb "ist" is in position 2, then the subject "die Lindenstraße", and "gesperrt" at the end.

questions.stem: The book title "Der Dativ ist dem Genitiv sein Tod" is a joke. What construction does it use?
choices: a genitive preposition with the dative
the possessive dative, a spoken way of showing possession
questions.explanation: "dem Genitiv sein Tod" (instead of "der Tod des Genitivs") is the possessive dative: dative + possessive + noun, as in "dem Vater sein Haus". It is common in everyday speech in many regions but not standard, so using it in a title that defends the genitive is the joke.

questions.stem: Which statement matches what the lesson says about the genitive debate?
choices: Linguists agree that the genitive will disappear from writing soon.
The possessive dative is correct in formal letters.
wegen with the dative means something different from wegen with the genitive.
In letters and exams the genitive is still the safe choice after nouns and after wegen, trotz and aufgrund.
questions.explanation: Whatever one thinks about language change, the practical rule is to write the genitive. Many linguists see change, not decay, and say the genitive is still normal in writing; the possessive dative is not standard; and wegen means the same with either case.

questions.stem: Complete with one preposition each: "___ des Stadtjubiläums gibt es ein großes Fest." (on the occasion of) and "___ Polizei gab es keine Verletzten." (according to)
questions.explanation: "anlässlich" (+ genitive) means on the occasion of: anlässlich des Stadtjubiläums. "laut" means according to; with a noun without an article there is no ending: laut Polizei.

questions.stem: Join the sentences: "Ich habe mit Herrn Kaya gesprochen. Sein Grundstück liegt direkt an der Baustelle." Which is correct?
choices: Ich habe mit Herrn Kaya gesprochen, deren Grundstück direkt an der Baustelle liegt.
Ich habe mit Herrn Kaya gesprochen, dessen Grundstück liegt direkt an der Baustelle.
Ich habe mit Herrn Kaya gesprochen, dessen das Grundstück direkt an der Baustelle liegt.
Ich habe mit Herrn Kaya gesprochen, dessen Grundstück direkt an der Baustelle liegt.
questions.explanation: The owner is masculine, so "dessen"; no article after it; and in the relative clause the verb goes to the end. "deren" is for a feminine or plural owner, the second choice keeps main-clause word order, and the third adds an article.

questions.stem: Complete with the present passive of "sortieren": "Das Altglas ___ nach Farben ___."
questions.explanation: The present passive is werden + Partizip II. "Das Altglas" is singular, so werden takes the er/sie/es form "wird" in position 2, and the participle "sortiert" (no ge- with -ieren verbs) goes to the end.

questions.stem: Put the words in order to say "Bikes are produced in this factory." The capitalised word comes first.
questions.explanation: "In dieser Fabrik" fills position 1, so the conjugated "werden" comes second, then the subject "Fahrräder", and the participle "produziert" goes to the very end. "werden" is plural because "Fahrräder" is plural.

questions.stem: Which sentences are correct? Select all that apply.
choices: Der Müll wird von der Stadt abgeholt.
Das Metall wird durch Magneten herausgezogen.
questions.explanation: "von der Stadt" (von + dative for an organisation) and "durch Magneten" (durch for a means) are both right. "Den Müll" keeps the accusative, but the passive subject must be nominative: "Der Müll wird abgeholt". "Die Flaschen" is plural, so "werden gesammelt". With man the verb is singular: "Man trennt den Müll".

questions.stem: Name the numbered rubbish containers.

image.alt: Five rubbish containers without names: a yellow bin for packaging, a blue bin for paper and cardboard, a brown bin for food scraps and garden waste, a grey bin for everything else, and a container with openings for white, green and brown glass. Each is numbered.

questions.explanation: Packaging goes in the yellow bin (die gelbe Tonne), paper and cardboard in the blue bin (die blaue Tonne), food and garden waste in the brown Biotonne, everything else in the grey Restmülltonne, and bottles and jars, sorted by colour, in the Altglascontainer. das Pfand is the deposit on bottles, and der Eimer is a bucket.

questions.stem: Match each sentence to the job that "werden" is doing in it.
left: Der Strom wird durch Windkraft erzeugt.
questions.explanation: Look at what goes with werden: an adjective or noun (teurer, Ingenieurin) means "become"; an infinitive (teurer werden) makes the future; a Partizip II (erzeugt, gebaut) makes the passive. werden never forms the perfect of other verbs.

questions.stem: Complete with "worden" or "geworden": "Mein Fahrrad ist gestohlen ___." "Sie ist Journalistin ___."
questions.explanation: The first sentence already has a participle (gestohlen), so it is the Perfekt passive and needs "worden". In the second, werden is the full verb "become" (she has become a journalist), so its participle is "geworden".

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this newspaper page.

image.alt: The front page of the Stadtanzeiger without labels: the date line, the headline Bäckerei durch Brand zerstört, a photo of a burning house, a caption in italics under the photo, and the article text. Five parts are numbered.

questions.explanation: 1 is the date (das Datum), 2 the headline (die Schlagzeile), 3 the photo (das Foto), 4 the caption under it (die Bildunterschrift) and 5 the article (der Artikel). There is no advert (die Anzeige) on the page, and a press conference is an event, not part of a page.

questions.stem: Finish the sentence "Ich habe gelesen, …" to say "that two paintings have been stolen". Put the words in order.
questions.explanation: After dass, the conjugated verb goes to the very end. The end of the clause is a chain: participle, worden, conjugated sein: "gestohlen worden sind".

questions.stem: Which sentences describe an action (an event), not a state? Select all that apply.
choices: Die Straße wurde um 8 Uhr gesperrt.
questions.explanation: wurde + participle and ist + participle + worden describe events: someone closed the road, opened the door, opened the bakery. "Die Straße ist gesperrt" and the sign "Heute geschlossen" are the state passive: they describe the situation now.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: aktuell is a false friend: it means "current, up to date", not "actual" (that is eigentlich or tatsächlich). "to invent" is erfinden.

questions.stem: Complete with the modal passive ("must be submitted"): "Der Antrag ___ bis Freitag eingereicht ___."
questions.explanation: The modal verb stands in position 2 and agrees with the subject (der Antrag: muss). At the end comes the passive infinitive: participle + werden, "eingereicht werden". Not "worden": that is only for the Perfekt passive.
